import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# First-move advantage in chess

What is the outcome of a perfectly played game of chess? Chess has not been solved: it is not
known whether perfect play by both sides leads to a win for White, a draw, or a win for Black.
The consensus among players and theorists (Steinitz, Lasker, Capablanca, Fischer, Kasparov,
Watson, Rowson, Short, ...) is that chess is a draw with best play.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, First-move advantage in chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/first-move_advantage_in_chess)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Solving chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solving_chess)
- [FIDE Laws of Chess](https://handbook.fide.com/chapter/E012023)

## The model

Mathlib has no model of chess, so this file formalises the FIDE Laws of Chess from scratch.
Files `a`–`h` and ranks `1`–`8` are indexed by `Fin 8`. A `Position` records the board, the
side to move, the castling rights, the en passant square and the half-move clock. A `Move` is
given by its source and destination squares together with an optional promotion piece; castling
is the king move of two squares along its home rank.

The following rules are formalised.
- Movement of the pieces, including pawn double steps, en passant, promotion and castling with
  all of its side conditions (FIDE Art. 3).
- A move is legal only if it does not leave the mover's own king in check (Art. 3.9).
- The game ends automatically with checkmate (Art. 5.1.1), stalemate (Art. 5.2.1), a dead
  position, in which no series of legal moves can lead to checkmate (Art. 5.2.2), the fivefold
  repetition of a position (Art. 9.6.1) and the 75-move rule (Art. 9.6.2), with checkmate taking
  precedence over the last two.
- The player having the move may claim a draw by threefold repetition (Art. 9.2) or by the
  50-move rule (Art. 9.3), either for the current position or for the position produced by a
  legal move. Two positions are the same in the sense of Art. 9.2.2 if they have the same board,
  the same side to move, the same castling rights and the same legal moves.

Resignation (Art. 5.1.2) and draw by agreement (Art. 5.2.3) are not modelled: resigning never
helps the resigning player, and a draw by agreement needs the consent of both players, so neither
changes what either side can force.

Chess is then a finite two-player game of perfect information: the 75-move rule bounds the length
of every game. A (pure) strategy for a player chooses an action in every state of the game where
that player has the move, and the outcome of a perfectly played game is determined by which player,
if any, has a strategy that forces a win. By Zermelo's theorem, exactly one of the following holds:
White can force a win, Black can force a win, or both players can force at least a draw.
-/

namespace FirstMoveAdvantageInChess

/- ### Pieces, squares and boards -/

/-- The two players. White moves first. -/
inductive Color
  | white
  | black
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- The opponent of a player. -/
def Color.other : Color → Color
  | .white => .black
  | .black => .white

/-- The six kinds of chess pieces. -/
inductive PieceType
  | king
  | queen
  | rook
  | bishop
  | knight
  | pawn
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- A chess piece: a kind of piece together with its colour. -/
structure Piece where
  color : Color
  type : PieceType
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- A square of the chessboard. Files `a`–`h` are `0`–`7` and ranks `1`–`8` are `0`–`7`,
so `⟨4, 0⟩` is the square `e1`. -/
structure Square where
  file : Fin 8
  rank : Fin 8
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- A chessboard, given by the piece standing on each square (if any). -/
abbrev Board := Square → Option Piece

/-- The two sides on which a player can castle. -/
inductive CastlingSide
  | kingside
  | queenside
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- The signed file difference from `a` to `b`. -/
def Square.df (a b : Square) : ℤ := (b.file : ℤ) - a.file

/-- The signed rank difference from `a` to `b`. -/
def Square.dr (a b : Square) : ℤ := (b.rank : ℤ) - a.rank

/-- The Chebyshev distance between two squares: the number of king steps needed to go from one
to the other. -/
def Square.dist (a b : Square) : ℕ := max (a.df b).natAbs (a.dr b).natAbs

/-- `b` is one king step away from `a`: it is an adjacent square (Art. 3.8.1). -/
def Square.IsKingStep (a b : Square) : Prop := a.dist b = 1

/-- `b` is one knight move away from `a`: the file and rank differences are `1` and `2`
in some order (Art. 3.6). -/
def Square.IsKnightStep (a b : Square) : Prop := (a.df b).natAbs * (a.dr b).natAbs = 2

/-- `a` and `b` are distinct squares on a common rank or file (Art. 3.3). -/
def Square.IsOrthogonal (a b : Square) : Prop := a ≠ b ∧ (a.df b = 0 ∨ a.dr b = 0)

/-- `a` and `b` are distinct squares on a common diagonal (Art. 3.2). -/
def Square.IsDiagonal (a b : Square) : Prop := a ≠ b ∧ (a.df b).natAbs = (a.dr b).natAbs

/-- `q` lies strictly between `a` and `b` on the rank, file or diagonal joining `a` and `b`:
it is reached from `a` by `k` steps towards `b`, where `0 < k < a.dist b`. -/
def Square.Between (a b q : Square) : Prop :=
  ∃ k < a.dist b, 0 < k ∧ (q.file : ℤ) = a.file + k * (a.df b).sign ∧
    (q.rank : ℤ) = a.rank + k * (a.dr b).sign

/-- All squares strictly between `a` and `b` are empty. -/
def Board.PathClear (board : Board) (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  ∀ q, a.Between b q → board q = none

/-- The direction in which the pawns of a player move: White's pawns move towards higher
ranks and Black's pawns towards lower ranks. -/
def Color.pawnDir : Color → ℤ
  | .white => 1
  | .black => -1

/-- The rank on which the pawns of a player start (the second and seventh ranks). -/
def Color.pawnStartRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 1
  | .black => 6

/-- The rank on which the pawns of a player promote (the eighth and first ranks). -/
def Color.promotionRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 7
  | .black => 0

/-- The rank on which the pieces of a player start (the first and eighth ranks). -/
def Color.homeRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 0
  | .black => 7

/-- The original square of the king of a player (`e1` or `e8`). -/
def Color.kingHome (c : Color) : Square := ⟨4, c.homeRank⟩

/-- The file of the rook with which one castles on the given side (`h` or `a`). -/
def CastlingSide.rookFile : CastlingSide → Fin 8
  | .kingside => 7
  | .queenside => 0

/-- The file on which the king lands when castling on the given side (`g` or `c`). -/
def CastlingSide.kingTargetFile : CastlingSide → Fin 8
  | .kingside => 6
  | .queenside => 2

/-- The file on which the rook lands when castling on the given side (`f` or `d`). This is
also the file of the square the king crosses. -/
def CastlingSide.rookTargetFile : CastlingSide → Fin 8
  | .kingside => 5
  | .queenside => 3

/-- The original square of the rook of player `c` on the side `s` (`h1`, `a1`, `h8` or `a8`). -/
def Color.rookHome (c : Color) (s : CastlingSide) : Square := ⟨s.rookFile, c.homeRank⟩

/-- The piece `p` standing on `a` attacks the square `b` on `board` (Art. 3.1), regardless of
what stands on `b`. Queens, rooks and bishops attack along lines that are not obstructed; pawns
attack the two squares diagonally in front of them. -/
def Board.PieceAttacks (board : Board) (p : Piece) (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  match p.type with
  | .king => a.IsKingStep b
  | .queen => (a.IsOrthogonal b ∨ a.IsDiagonal b) ∧ board.PathClear a b
  | .rook => a.IsOrthogonal b ∧ board.PathClear a b
  | .bishop => a.IsDiagonal b ∧ board.PathClear a b
  | .knight => a.IsKnightStep b
  | .pawn => (a.df b).natAbs = 1 ∧ a.dr b = p.color.pawnDir

/-- The square `sq` is attacked by some piece of colour `c`. -/
def Board.Attacked (board : Board) (c : Color) (sq : Square) : Prop :=
  ∃ a p, board a = some p ∧ p.color = c ∧ board.PieceAttacks p a sq

/-- The king of colour `c` is in check: it is attacked by a piece of the opponent (Art. 3.9). -/
def Board.InCheck (board : Board) (c : Color) : Prop :=
  ∃ sq, board sq = some ⟨c, .king⟩ ∧ board.Attacked c.other sq

/- ### Positions and moves -/

/-- The state of a game of chess between two moves, as far as it is relevant for the
legal moves. -/
structure Position where
  /-- The pieces on the board. -/
  board : Board
  /-- The player having the move. -/
  turn : Color
  /-- `castling c s` holds if player `c` still has the right to castle on the side `s`, that is,
  neither the king nor the rook on that side has moved (Art. 3.8.2.1). -/
  castling : Color → CastlingSide → Bool
  /-- If the last move was a pawn advance of two squares, the square that the pawn passed over,
  onto which an en passant capture would go (Art. 3.7.4.1). Otherwise `none`. -/
  enPassant : Option Square
  /-- The number of moves by either player since the last capture or pawn move. -/
  halfmoveClock : ℕ

/-- A move: the square the moving piece leaves, the square it goes to, and, for a pawn reaching
the last rank, the kind of piece it is promoted to (Art. 3.7.5.1). Castling is written as the
king move of two squares along its home rank. -/
structure Move where
  src : Square
  dst : Square
  promotion : Option PieceType
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The move `m` is made by a pawn of the side to move. -/
def Position.MovesPawn (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  pos.board m.src = some ⟨pos.turn, .pawn⟩

instance (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Decidable (pos.MovesPawn m) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ = _))

/-- The move `m` captures the piece standing on its destination square. -/
def Position.Captures (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  pos.board m.dst ≠ none

instance (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Decidable (pos.Captures m) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ≠ _))

/-- The move `m` is an en passant capture: a pawn moves diagonally onto the en passant square. -/
def Position.IsEnPassant (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  pos.MovesPawn m ∧ pos.enPassant = some m.dst ∧ m.src.file ≠ m.dst.file

instance (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Decidable (pos.IsEnPassant m) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _ ∧ _))

/-- If `m` moves the king of the side to move two squares along its home rank from its original
square, the side on which it castles; otherwise `none`. -/
def Position.castlingSide? (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Option CastlingSide :=
  if pos.board m.src = some ⟨pos.turn, .king⟩ ∧ m.src = pos.turn.kingHome ∧
      m.dst.rank = pos.turn.homeRank then
    if m.dst.file = CastlingSide.kingside.kingTargetFile then some .kingside
    else if m.dst.file = CastlingSide.queenside.kingTargetFile then some .queenside
    else none
  else none

/-- The move `m` is a legal castling on the side `s` (Art. 3.8.2), apart from the general
condition that the king is not left in check: the side to move still has the right to castle on
that side, its king and rook stand on their original squares with nothing between them, and neither
the square of the king, nor the square it crosses, nor the square it lands on is attacked. -/
def Position.IsCastling (pos : Position) (m : Move) (s : CastlingSide) : Prop :=
  pos.castlingSide? m = some s ∧ pos.castling pos.turn s = true ∧ m.promotion = none ∧
    pos.board (pos.turn.rookHome s) = some ⟨pos.turn, .rook⟩ ∧
    pos.board.PathClear pos.turn.kingHome (pos.turn.rookHome s) ∧
    ¬ pos.board.Attacked pos.turn.other pos.turn.kingHome ∧
    ¬ pos.board.Attacked pos.turn.other ⟨s.rookTargetFile, pos.turn.homeRank⟩ ∧
    ¬ pos.board.Attacked pos.turn.other m.dst

/-- The move `m` moves a pawn of the side to move according to Art. 3.7: one square forward onto
an empty square; two squares forward from its starting rank over an empty square onto an empty
square; one square diagonally forward capturing an opponent's piece; or an en passant capture.
A pawn reaching the last rank must be promoted to a queen, rook, bishop or knight, and no other
move is a promotion. -/
def Position.IsPawnMove (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  ((m.src.df m.dst = 0 ∧ m.src.dr m.dst = pos.turn.pawnDir ∧ pos.board m.dst = none) ∨
    (m.src.df m.dst = 0 ∧ m.src.dr m.dst = 2 * pos.turn.pawnDir ∧
      m.src.rank = pos.turn.pawnStartRank ∧ pos.board.PathClear m.src m.dst ∧
      pos.board m.dst = none) ∨
    ((m.src.df m.dst).natAbs = 1 ∧ m.src.dr m.dst = pos.turn.pawnDir ∧
      ∃ q, pos.board m.dst = some q ∧ q.color = pos.turn.other) ∨
    ((m.src.df m.dst).natAbs = 1 ∧ m.src.dr m.dst = pos.turn.pawnDir ∧ pos.IsEnPassant m ∧
      pos.board m.dst = none ∧
      pos.board ⟨m.dst.file, m.src.rank⟩ = some ⟨pos.turn.other, .pawn⟩)) ∧
  match m.promotion with
  | none => m.dst.rank ≠ pos.turn.promotionRank
  | some t => m.dst.rank = pos.turn.promotionRank ∧ t ≠ .king ∧ t ≠ .pawn

/-- The move `m` follows the movement rules of Art. 3: it moves a piece of the side to move in
the way that piece moves, onto a square not occupied by a piece of the same colour. Whether the
move leaves the own king in check is not taken into account. -/
def Position.IsPseudoLegal (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  ∃ p, pos.board m.src = some p ∧ p.color = pos.turn ∧
    (∀ q, pos.board m.dst = some q → q.color ≠ pos.turn) ∧
    match p.type with
    | .pawn => pos.IsPawnMove m
    | .king => (m.src.IsKingStep m.dst ∧ m.promotion = none) ∨ ∃ s, pos.IsCastling m s
    | _ => pos.board.PieceAttacks p m.src m.dst ∧ m.promotion = none

/-- The position after the move `m` is made in `pos`. The moving piece (or the piece it is
promoted to) is placed on the destination square; when castling, the rook is moved to the square
the king crossed; in an en passant capture, the captured pawn is removed. Castling rights are lost
when the king moves and when a rook moves from or is captured on its original square. The en
passant square is set after a pawn advance of two squares. The half-move clock is reset by a
pawn move or a capture and otherwise increased by one. -/
def Position.play (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Position where
  board q :=
    if q = m.src then none
    else if q = m.dst then
      match m.promotion with
      | some t => some ⟨pos.turn, t⟩
      | none => pos.board m.src
    else
      match pos.castlingSide? m with
      | some s =>
        if q = pos.turn.rookHome s then none
        else if q = ⟨s.rookTargetFile, pos.turn.homeRank⟩ then some ⟨pos.turn, .rook⟩
        else pos.board q
      | none =>
        if pos.IsEnPassant m ∧ q = ⟨m.dst.file, m.src.rank⟩ then none
        else pos.board q
  turn := pos.turn.other
  castling c s :=
    pos.castling c s && m.src != c.kingHome && m.src != c.rookHome s && m.dst != c.rookHome s
  enPassant :=
    if pos.MovesPawn m ∧ (m.src.dr m.dst).natAbs = 2 then
      some ⟨m.src.file, ⟨(m.src.rank.val + m.dst.rank.val) / 2, by omega⟩⟩
    else none
  halfmoveClock := if pos.MovesPawn m ∨ pos.Captures m then 0 else pos.halfmoveClock + 1

/-- The move `m` is legal in `pos`: it follows the movement rules and does not leave the own
king in check (Art. 3.9.2). -/
def Position.IsLegal (pos : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  pos.IsPseudoLegal m ∧ ¬ (pos.play m).board.InCheck pos.turn

/-- The side to move is checkmated: its king is in check and it has no legal move
(Art. 1.4.1). -/
def Position.IsCheckmate (pos : Position) : Prop :=
  pos.board.InCheck pos.turn ∧ ∀ m, ¬ pos.IsLegal m

/-- The side to move is stalemated: its king is not in check and it has no legal move
(Art. 5.2.1). -/
def Position.IsStalemate (pos : Position) : Prop :=
  ¬ pos.board.InCheck pos.turn ∧ ∀ m, ¬ pos.IsLegal m

/-- `q` is obtained from `p` by one legal move. -/
def Position.Step (p q : Position) : Prop :=
  ∃ m, p.IsLegal m ∧ q = p.play m

/-- `pos` is a dead position: no series of legal moves can lead to checkmate (Art. 5.2.2). -/
def Position.IsDead (pos : Position) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ q, Relation.ReflTransGen Position.Step pos q ∧ q.IsCheckmate

/-- Two positions are the same in the sense of Art. 9.2.2: the same player has the move, pieces
of the same kind and colour occupy the same squares, the castling rights are the same, and the
possible moves are the same (so that they agree on whether an en passant capture is possible). -/
def Position.Same (p q : Position) : Prop :=
  p.board = q.board ∧ p.turn = q.turn ∧ p.castling = q.castling ∧
    ∀ m, p.IsLegal m ↔ q.IsLegal m

/-- The pieces on the first rank in the initial position, from the `a`-file to the `h`-file. -/
def backRank : Fin 8 → PieceType :=
  ![.rook, .knight, .bishop, .queen, .king, .bishop, .knight, .rook]

/-- The initial position of the pieces (Art. 2.3). -/
def initialBoard : Board := fun sq =>
  if sq.rank = 0 then some ⟨.white, backRank sq.file⟩
  else if sq.rank = 1 then some ⟨.white, .pawn⟩
  else if sq.rank = 6 then some ⟨.black, .pawn⟩
  else if sq.rank = 7 then some ⟨.black, backRank sq.file⟩
  else none

/-- The initial position: White is to move, both players may castle on both sides. -/
def initialPosition : Position where
  board := initialBoard
  turn := .white
  castling _ _ := true
  enPassant := none
  halfmoveClock := 0

/-- In the initial position White may play the pawn from `e2` to `e4`. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem initialPosition_isLegal_e2e4 :
    initialPosition.IsLegal ⟨⟨4, 1⟩, ⟨4, 3⟩, none⟩ := by
  sorry

/-- In the initial position White may not castle. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem initialPosition_not_isLegal_castling :
    ¬ initialPosition.IsLegal ⟨⟨4, 0⟩, ⟨6, 0⟩, none⟩ := by
  sorry

/-- Fool's mate: after `1. f3 e5 2. g4 Qh4#` White is checkmated. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem foolsMate_isCheckmate :
    ((((initialPosition.play ⟨⟨5, 1⟩, ⟨5, 2⟩, none⟩).play
      ⟨⟨4, 6⟩, ⟨4, 4⟩, none⟩).play
      ⟨⟨6, 1⟩, ⟨6, 3⟩, none⟩).play
      ⟨⟨3, 7⟩, ⟨7, 3⟩, none⟩).IsCheckmate := by
  sorry

/- ### Games, strategies and the value of chess -/

/-- The state of a game: the current position, the earlier positions of the game (needed for
the repetition rules), and whether the game has been ended by a draw claim. -/
structure GameState where
  /-- The current position. -/
  pos : Position
  /-- The earlier positions of the game, most recent first. -/
  past : List Position
  /-- The game has been ended by a claim of a draw (Art. 9.2 or 9.3). -/
  drawClaimed : Bool

/-- The state of the game at the start. -/
def initialState : GameState where
  pos := initialPosition
  past := []
  drawClaimed := false

/-- The state after the move `m` is made. -/
def GameState.playMove (s : GameState) (m : Move) : GameState where
  pos := s.pos.play m
  past := s.pos :: s.past
  drawClaimed := false

open scoped Classical in
/-- The number of times the current position has appeared in the game, in the sense of
Art. 9.2.2, counting the current occurrence. -/
noncomputable def GameState.repetitions (s : GameState) : ℕ :=
  1 + s.past.countP fun q => decide (s.pos.Same q)

/-- The current position is one for which a draw can be claimed: it has appeared at least three
times (Art. 9.2.1) or the last 50 moves by each player were made without a pawn move or a capture
(Art. 9.3.1). -/
def GameState.IsClaimable (s : GameState) : Prop :=
  3 ≤ s.repetitions ∨ 100 ≤ s.pos.halfmoveClock

/-- The player having the move can claim a draw: either the current position is claimable
(Art. 9.2.1.2 and 9.3.1.2), or the player has a legal move that produces a claimable position
(Art. 9.2.1.1 and 9.3.1.1). -/
def GameState.CanClaimDraw (s : GameState) : Prop :=
  s.IsClaimable ∨ ∃ m, s.pos.IsLegal m ∧ (s.playMove m).IsClaimable

/-- The game has been won by `c`: the opponent of `c` is to move and is checkmated
(Art. 5.1.1). -/
def GameState.IsWinFor (s : GameState) (c : Color) : Prop :=
  s.pos.IsCheckmate ∧ s.pos.turn = c.other

/-- The game is over: a draw has been claimed, or the side to move is checkmated or stalemated,
or the position is dead, or the same position has appeared at least five times (Art. 9.6.1), or
the last 75 moves by each player were made without a pawn move or a capture (Art. 9.6.2). -/
def GameState.IsOver (s : GameState) : Prop :=
  s.drawClaimed = true ∨ s.pos.IsCheckmate ∨ s.pos.IsStalemate ∨ s.pos.IsDead ∨
    5 ≤ s.repetitions ∨ 150 ≤ s.pos.halfmoveClock

/-- An action of the player having the move: make a move, or claim a draw. -/
inductive Action
  | move (m : Move)
  | claimDraw

/-- The action `a` is allowed in the state `s`. -/
def GameState.IsLegalAction (s : GameState) : Action → Prop
  | .move m => s.pos.IsLegal m
  | .claimDraw => s.CanClaimDraw

/-- The state after the action `a` is taken in the state `s`. -/
def GameState.step (s : GameState) : Action → GameState
  | .move m => s.playMove m
  | .claimDraw => { s with drawClaimed := true }

/-- A strategy: a choice of action in every state of the game. Only the values at states where
the game is not over and the strategy's owner has the move matter. -/
def Strategy := GameState → Action

/-- The strategy `σ` is a legal strategy for the player `c`: whenever `c` has the move and the
game is not over, it chooses an allowed action. -/
def Strategy.IsLegal (σ : Strategy) (c : Color) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : GameState, s.pos.turn = c → ¬ s.IsOver → s.IsLegalAction (σ s)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The game played from the initial position when each player `c` follows the strategy
`σ c`: `play σ n` is the state after `n` actions. Once the game is over the state no longer
changes. -/
noncomputable def play (σ : Color → Strategy) : ℕ → GameState
  | 0 => initialState
  | n + 1 =>
    let s := play σ n
    if s.IsOver then s else s.step (σ s.pos.turn s)

/-- The player `c` can force a win: `c` has a legal strategy such that, against every legal
strategy of the opponent, the game ends with `c` checkmating the opponent. -/
def CanForceWin (c : Color) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : Strategy, σ.IsLegal c ∧ ∀ τ : Strategy, τ.IsLegal c.other →
    ∃ n, (play (fun d => if d = c then σ else τ) n).IsWinFor c

/-- The player `c` can force at least a draw: `c` has a legal strategy such that, against every
legal strategy of the opponent, `c` is never checkmated. -/
def CanForceDraw (c : Color) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : Strategy, σ.IsLegal c ∧ ∀ τ : Strategy, τ.IsLegal c.other →
    ∀ n, ¬ (play (fun d => if d = c then σ else τ) n).IsWinFor c.other

/-- The outcome of a perfectly played game of chess, that is, the game-theoretic value of chess:
a win for White if White can force a win, a win for Black if Black can force a win, and a draw
otherwise. By Zermelo's theorem the game is determined, so in the last case both players can force
at least a draw (see `perfectPlayOutcome_eq_draw_iff`). -/
noncomputable def perfectPlayOutcome : Outcome :=
  if CanForceWin .white then .win .white
  else if CanForceWin .black then .win .black
  else .draw

/-- Chess is a finite game of perfect information, so by Zermelo's theorem it is determined:
its value is a draw if and only if both players can force at least a draw. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem perfectPlayOutcome_eq_draw_iff :
    perfectPlayOutcome = .draw ↔ CanForceDraw .white ∧ CanForceDraw .black := by
  sorry

a win for White, a draw, or a win for Black? Chess has not been solved, so the game-theoretic
value of chess (from the standard initial position, under the FIDE Laws of Chess) is unknown. -/
@[category research open, AMS 91]

chess is a draw: neither White nor Black can force a win. -/

/-!
# First-move advantage in chess

This file models chess from the standard initial position. Games have no clock and end under the
FIDE over-the-board rules, including checkmate, stalemate, dead positions, and the automatic
75-move and fivefold-repetition draws. The claimable 50-move and threefold-repetition
rules are modeled as history-dependent choices. Draw offers are omitted because they do not change
the perfect-play value.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, First-move advantage in chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/first-move_advantage_in_chess)
- [FIDE, Laws of Chess](https://handbook.fide.com/chapter/E012023)

namespace FirstMoveAdvantageInChess

noncomputable section

local instance (p : Prop) : Decidable p := Classical.propDecidable p

inductive Color
  | white
  | black
  deriving DecidableEq

inductive PieceKind
  | king
  | queen
  | rook
  | bishop
  | knight
  | pawn
  deriving DecidableEq

structure Piece where
  color : Color
  kind : PieceKind
  deriving DecidableEq

structure Square where
  file : Fin 8
  rank : Fin 8
  deriving DecidableEq

abbrev Board := Square → Option Piece

def Color.other : Color → Color
  | .white => .black
  | .black => .white

structure CastlingRights where
  whiteKingSide : Bool
  whiteQueenSide : Bool
  blackKingSide : Bool
  blackQueenSide : Bool
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A position records the information relevant to legal play. `halfmoveClock` counts plies since
    the last capture or pawn move. -/
structure Position where
  board : Board
  turn : Color
  rights : CastlingRights
  enPassant : Option Square
  halfmoveClock : ℕ
  drawClaimed : Bool

local instance : DecidableEq Position := Classical.decEq _

structure Move where
  src : Square
  dst : Square
  promotion : Option PieceKind := none
  deriving DecidableEq

private def iFile (s : Square) : ℤ := s.file.val
private def iRank (s : Square) : ℤ := s.rank.val

private def diagonal (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  |iFile b - iFile a| = |iRank b - iRank a|

private def orthogonal (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  a.file = b.file ∨ a.rank = b.rank

private def strictlyBetween (a b c : ℤ) : Prop :=
  (a < b ∧ b < c) ∨ (c < b ∧ b < a)

private def between (a x b : Square) : Prop :=
  (a.file = b.file ∧ x.file = a.file ∧ strictlyBetween (iRank a) (iRank x) (iRank b)) ∨
  (a.rank = b.rank ∧ x.rank = a.rank ∧ strictlyBetween (iFile a) (iFile x) (iFile b)) ∨
  (diagonal a b ∧ diagonal a x ∧ strictlyBetween (iFile a) (iFile x) (iFile b) ∧
    strictlyBetween (iRank a) (iRank x) (iRank b))

private def pathClear (b : Board) (a z : Square) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, between a x z → b x = none

private def pawnAttacks (c : Color) (a z : Square) : Prop :=
  |iFile z - iFile a| = 1 ∧
    match c with
    | .white => z.rank.val = a.rank.val + 1
    | .black => a.rank.val = z.rank.val + 1

private def attacksFrom (b : Board) (p : Piece) (a z : Square) : Prop :=
  a ≠ z ∧ match p.kind with
  | .king => |iFile z - iFile a| ≤ 1 ∧ |iRank z - iRank a| ≤ 1
  | .queen => (orthogonal a z ∨ diagonal a z) ∧ pathClear b a z
  | .rook => orthogonal a z ∧ pathClear b a z
  | .bishop => diagonal a z ∧ pathClear b a z
  | .knight =>
      (|iFile z - iFile a| = 1 ∧ |iRank z - iRank a| = 2) ∨
      (|iFile z - iFile a| = 2 ∧ |iRank z - iRank a| = 1)
  | .pawn => pawnAttacks p.color a z

private def Attacked (b : Board) (c : Color) (z : Square) : Prop :=
  ∃ a p, b a = some p ∧ p.color = c ∧ attacksFrom b p a z

private def InCheck (b : Board) (c : Color) : Prop :=
  ∃ k, b k = some ⟨c, .king⟩ ∧ Attacked b c.other k

private def initialKind (f : Fin 8) : PieceKind :=
  if f.val = 0 ∨ f.val = 7 then .rook
  else if f.val = 1 ∨ f.val = 6 then .knight
  else if f.val = 2 ∨ f.val = 5 then .bishop
  else if f.val = 3 then .queen else .king

/-- The usual initial chess position, with White moving towards increasing ranks. -/
def initialBoard : Board := fun s =>
  if s.rank.val = 0 then some ⟨.white, initialKind s.file⟩
  else if s.rank.val = 1 then some ⟨.white, .pawn⟩
  else if s.rank.val = 6 then some ⟨.black, .pawn⟩
  else if s.rank.val = 7 then some ⟨.black, initialKind s.file⟩
  else none

/-- The standard initial position. -/
def initialPosition : Position where
  board := initialBoard
  turn := .white
  rights := ⟨true, true, true, true⟩
  enPassant := none
  halfmoveClock := 0
  drawClaimed := false

private def homeKing (c : Color) : Square :=
  ⟨4, if c = .white then 0 else 7⟩

private def homeRook (c : Color) (kingSide : Bool) : Square :=
  ⟨if kingSide then 7 else 0, if c = .white then 0 else 7⟩

private def castleKingTo (c : Color) (kingSide : Bool) : Square :=
  ⟨if kingSide then 6 else 2, if c = .white then 0 else 7⟩

private def castleRookTo (c : Color) (kingSide : Bool) : Square :=
  ⟨if kingSide then 5 else 3, if c = .white then 0 else 7⟩

private def hasRight (r : CastlingRights) (c : Color) (kingSide : Bool) : Bool :=
  match c, kingSide with
  | .white, true => r.whiteKingSide
  | .white, false => r.whiteQueenSide
  | .black, true => r.blackKingSide
  | .black, false => r.blackQueenSide

private def revokeColor (r : CastlingRights) (c : Color) : CastlingRights :=
  match c with
  | .white => { r with whiteKingSide := false, whiteQueenSide := false }
  | .black => { r with blackKingSide := false, blackQueenSide := false }

private def revokeRookSquare (r : CastlingRights) (s : Square) : CastlingRights :=
  if s = homeRook .white true then { r with whiteKingSide := false }
  else if s = homeRook .white false then { r with whiteQueenSide := false }
  else if s = homeRook .black true then { r with blackKingSide := false }
  else if s = homeRook .black false then { r with blackQueenSide := false }
  else r

private def nextRights (r : CastlingRights) (p : Piece) (src captured : Square) : CastlingRights :=
  let r' := if p.kind = .king then revokeColor r p.color else revokeRookSquare r src
  revokeRookSquare r' captured

private def isPromotionKind : PieceKind → Prop
  | .queen | .rook | .bishop | .knight => True
  | _ => False

private def reachesLastRank (c : Color) (s : Square) : Prop :=
  match c with
  | .white => s.rank.val = 7
  | .black => s.rank.val = 0

private def pawnForwardOne (c : Color) (a z : Square) : Prop :=
  a.file = z.file ∧ match c with
  | .white => z.rank.val = a.rank.val + 1
  | .black => a.rank.val = z.rank.val + 1

private def pawnForwardTwo (c : Color) (a z : Square) : Prop :=
  a.file = z.file ∧ match c with
  | .white => a.rank.val = 1 ∧ z.rank.val = 3
  | .black => a.rank.val = 6 ∧ z.rank.val = 4

private def passedSquare (c : Color) (a : Square) : Square :=
  match c with
  | .white => ⟨a.file, ⟨(a.rank.val + 1) % 8, Nat.mod_lt _ (by omega)⟩⟩
  | .black => ⟨a.file, ⟨(a.rank.val + 7) % 8, Nat.mod_lt _ (by omega)⟩⟩

private def capturedSquare (s : Position) (m : Move) : Square :=
  if s.board m.dst = none ∧ (s.board m.src).any (fun p => p.kind = .pawn) ∧
      m.src.file ≠ m.dst.file then ⟨m.dst.file, m.src.rank⟩ else m.dst

private def movedPiece (p : Piece) (m : Move) : Piece :=
  match m.promotion with
  | some k => ⟨p.color, k⟩
  | none => p

private def moveBoard (s : Position) (m : Move) (p : Piece) : Board := fun x =>
  if x = m.dst then some (movedPiece p m)
  else if x = m.src ∨ x = capturedSquare s m then none
  else s.board x

private def ordinaryGeometry (s : Position) (m : Move) (p : Piece) : Prop :=
  m.src ≠ m.dst ∧ match p.kind with
  | .king => |iFile m.dst - iFile m.src| ≤ 1 ∧ |iRank m.dst - iRank m.src| ≤ 1
  | .queen => (orthogonal m.src m.dst ∨ diagonal m.src m.dst) ∧
      pathClear s.board m.src m.dst
  | .rook => orthogonal m.src m.dst ∧ pathClear s.board m.src m.dst
  | .bishop => diagonal m.src m.dst ∧ pathClear s.board m.src m.dst
  | .knight =>
      (|iFile m.dst - iFile m.src| = 1 ∧ |iRank m.dst - iRank m.src| = 2) ∨
      (|iFile m.dst - iFile m.src| = 2 ∧ |iRank m.dst - iRank m.src| = 1)
  | .pawn =>
      (pawnForwardOne p.color m.src m.dst ∧ s.board m.dst = none) ∨
      (pawnForwardTwo p.color m.src m.dst ∧ s.board m.dst = none ∧
        s.board (passedSquare p.color m.src) = none) ∨
      (pawnAttacks p.color m.src m.dst ∧
        ((∃ q, s.board m.dst = some q ∧ q.color = p.color.other ∧ q.kind ≠ .king) ∨
         (s.enPassant = some m.dst ∧ s.board m.dst = none ∧
          s.board ⟨m.dst.file, m.src.rank⟩ = some ⟨p.color.other, .pawn⟩)))

private def promotionCorrect (p : Piece) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  if p.kind = .pawn ∧ reachesLastRank p.color m.dst then
    ∃ k, m.promotion = some k ∧ isPromotionKind k
  else m.promotion = none

private def OrdinaryMoveWith (s : Position) (m : Move) (t : Position) : Prop :=
  ∃ p,
    s.board m.src = some p ∧ p.color = s.turn ∧
    (∀ q, s.board m.dst = some q → q.color ≠ p.color ∧ q.kind ≠ .king) ∧
    ordinaryGeometry s m p ∧ promotionCorrect p m ∧
    let b' := moveBoard s m p
    ¬ InCheck b' p.color ∧
    t = { board := b'
          turn := s.turn.other
          rights := nextRights s.rights p m.src (capturedSquare s m)
          enPassant := if p.kind = .pawn ∧ pawnForwardTwo p.color m.src m.dst
            then some (passedSquare p.color m.src) else none
          halfmoveClock := if p.kind = .pawn ∨ s.board (capturedSquare s m) ≠ none
            then 0 else s.halfmoveClock + 1
          drawClaimed := false }

private def OrdinaryMove (s t : Position) : Prop :=
  ∃ m, OrdinaryMoveWith s m t

private def castleBoard (s : Position) (kingSide : Bool) : Board := fun x =>
  if x = homeKing s.turn ∨ x = homeRook s.turn kingSide then none
  else if x = castleKingTo s.turn kingSide then some ⟨s.turn, .king⟩
  else if x = castleRookTo s.turn kingSide then some ⟨s.turn, .rook⟩
  else s.board x

private def CastleMove (s t : Position) : Prop :=
  ∃ kingSide : Bool,
    hasRight s.rights s.turn kingSide = true ∧
    s.board (homeKing s.turn) = some ⟨s.turn, .king⟩ ∧
    s.board (homeRook s.turn kingSide) = some ⟨s.turn, .rook⟩ ∧
    pathClear s.board (homeKing s.turn) (homeRook s.turn kingSide) ∧
    ¬ Attacked s.board s.turn.other (homeKing s.turn) ∧
    ¬ Attacked s.board s.turn.other (castleRookTo s.turn kingSide) ∧
    ¬ Attacked (castleBoard s kingSide) s.turn.other (castleKingTo s.turn kingSide) ∧
    t = { board := castleBoard s kingSide
          turn := s.turn.other
          rights := revokeColor s.rights s.turn
          enPassant := none
          halfmoveClock := s.halfmoveClock + 1
          drawClaimed := false }

/-- One legal chess move, before applying any automatic game-ending rule. -/
def LegalMove (s t : Position) : Prop := OrdinaryMove s t ∨ CastleMove s t

private def Checkmate (s : Position) : Prop :=
  InCheck s.board s.turn ∧ ¬ ∃ t, LegalMove s t

private def Stalemate (s : Position) : Prop :=
  ¬ InCheck s.board s.turn ∧ ¬ ∃ t, LegalMove s t

/-- A dead position is one from which no sequence of legal moves can produce checkmate. -/
def DeadPosition (s : Position) : Prop :=
  ∀ t, Relation.ReflTransGen LegalMove s t → ¬ Checkmate t

private def enPassantAvailable (s : Position) (q : Square) : Prop :=
  s.enPassant = some q ∧ ∃ a t, s.board a = some ⟨s.turn, .pawn⟩ ∧
    a.file ≠ q.file ∧ s.board q = none ∧
    OrdinaryMoveWith s { src := a, dst := q, promotion := none } t

/-- Equality of positions for the FIDE repetition rule. The en-passant field matters exactly when
    an en-passant capture is actually available. -/
def SameForRepetition (s t : Position) : Prop :=
  s.board = t.board ∧ s.turn = t.turn ∧ s.rights = t.rights ∧
    ∀ q, enPassantAvailable s q ↔ enPassantAvailable t q

private def repetitionCount (h : List Position) (s : Position) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card {i : Fin h.length // SameForRepetition (h.get i) s}

inductive Outcome
  | whiteWin
  | draw
  | blackWin
  deriving DecidableEq

private def result? (h : List Position) : Option Outcome :=
  match h.getLast? with
  | none => none
  | some s =>
      if s.drawClaimed then some .draw
      else if Checkmate s then some (if s.turn = .white then .blackWin else .whiteWin)
      else if Stalemate s ∨ DeadPosition s ∨ 150 ≤ s.halfmoveClock ∨ 5 ≤ repetitionCount h s
      then some .draw else none

private def claimPosition (s : Position) : Position := { s with drawClaimed := true }

/-- A player may claim after a threefold repetition or 50 moves, or by recording a legal move
    which would reach one of those thresholds. -/
private def ClaimAvailable (h : List Position) (s : Position) : Prop :=
  3 ≤ repetitionCount (h ++ [s]) s ∨ 100 ≤ s.halfmoveClock ∨
    ∃ t, LegalMove s t ∧
      (3 ≤ repetitionCount (h ++ [s, t]) t ∨ 100 ≤ t.halfmoveClock)

private def HistoryStep (h : List Position) (s t : Position) : Prop :=
  LegalMove s t ∨ (ClaimAvailable h s ∧ t = claimPosition s)

/-- Histories are listed in chronological order and cannot continue after an automatic result. -/
inductive LegalHistory : List Position → Prop
  | initial : LegalHistory [initialPosition]
  | step {h s t} : LegalHistory (h ++ [s]) → result? (h ++ [s]) = none → HistoryStep h s t →
      LegalHistory (h ++ [s, t])

abbrev Strategy := List Position → Position

private def LegalStrategy (c : Color) (σ : Strategy) : Prop :=
  ∀ h s, LegalHistory (h ++ [s]) → result? (h ++ [s]) = none → s.turn = c →
    HistoryStep h s (σ (h ++ [s]))

private inductive Follows (white black : Strategy) : List Position → Prop
  | initial : Follows white black [initialPosition]
  | step {h s} : Follows white black (h ++ [s]) → result? (h ++ [s]) = none →
      Follows white black (h ++ [s, if s.turn = .white then white (h ++ [s]) else black (h ++ [s])])

private def CanForce (c : Color) (acceptable : Set Outcome) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ, LegalStrategy c σ ∧ ∀ τ, LegalStrategy c.other τ →
    ∃ h o, LegalHistory h ∧ Follows (if c = .white then σ else τ)
      (if c = .black then σ else τ) h ∧ result? h = some o ∧ o ∈ acceptable

/-- The game-theoretic value of chess from the standard initial position, from White's point of
    view. -/
noncomputable def chessValue : Outcome :=
  if CanForce .white {.whiteWin} then .whiteWin
  else if CanForce .black {.blackWin} then .blackWin
  else .draw

/--
With perfect play from the standard initial position under the FIDE rules, chess ends in a draw.
This is the consensus candidate answer to “What is the outcome of a perfectly played game of
chess?”
-/
@[category research open, AMS 91]
theorem first_move_advantage_in_chess : chessValue = .draw := by
  sorry

end

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# First-move advantage in chess

What is the outcome of a perfectly played game of chess?

Chess is a finite two-player zero-sum game of perfect information, so from the standard
initial position exactly one of the following holds: White can force a win, Black can force a
win, or neither can (and then both sides can force at least a draw). The game has not been
solved. The consensus among players and theorists since Steinitz (1889) is that the first move
gives White an advantage that is not large enough to win, i.e. that chess is a draw with best
play; a minority view (Adams, Berliner) holds that White wins.

This file formalises the rules of chess from the FIDE Laws of Chess and states the question.

## The model

* `Square`, `Piece`, `Board`, `Position`: the board, the side to move, castling rights and the
  square available for an en passant capture (Articles 2 and 3).
* `Position.IsLegal`: legal moves (Articles 3.1–3.10), including the double pawn advance,
  en passant captures, promotion and castling. A move may not leave one's own king in check.
* `GameState`: a position together with the number of half-moves since the last capture or pawn
  move and the list of previously occurring positions.
* `GameState.result`: the game ends with checkmate (Article 5.1.1), stalemate (5.2.1), a dead
  position (5.2.2), fivefold repetition (9.6.1) or the 75-move rule (9.6.2). Checkmate takes
  precedence over the 75-move rule.
* `GameState.CanClaimDraw`: the player to move may claim a draw by threefold repetition
  (Article 9.2) or by the 50-move rule (Article 9.3), either immediately or together with the
  move producing the repetition or the 50th move. Positions are the same in the sense of
  Article 9.2.2 (`Position.Same`).
* `CanForceWin c s`: player `c` can force a win from the game state `s`. This is the least
  predicate closed under the usual rules: a terminal state won by `c`; `c` to move with some
  legal move to a state from which `c` can force a win; the opponent to move, unable to claim a
  draw, with every legal move leading to a state from which `c` can force a win.
* `perfectPlayOutcome`: the outcome of the game with perfect play from the initial position.

Resignation (Article 5.1.2) and draws by agreement (Article 5.2.3) are omitted. They are
available to the players but cannot change the outcome under perfect play.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, First-move advantage in chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/first-move_advantage_in_chess)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Wikipedia, Solving chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solving_chess)
* [FIDE Laws of Chess](https://handbook.fide.com/chapter/E012023)
-/

namespace FirstMoveAdvantageInChess

/-- The two players. -/
inductive Color
  | white
  | black
deriving DecidableEq

/-- The opponent of a player. -/
def Color.other : Color → Color
  | .white => .black
  | .black => .white

/-- The direction (in ranks) in which the pawns of a player advance. -/
def Color.forward : Color → ℤ
  | .white => 1
  | .black => -1

/-- The rank on which the king and rooks of a player start. -/
def Color.homeRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 0
  | .black => 7

/-- The rank on which the pawns of a player start. -/
def Color.pawnRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 1
  | .black => 6

/-- The rank passed over by a pawn of a player advancing two squares. -/
def Color.passRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 2
  | .black => 5

/-- The rank furthest from the starting position of the pawns of a player. -/
def Color.promotionRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 7
  | .black => 0

/-- The kinds of pieces. -/
inductive PieceType
  | king
  | queen
  | rook
  | bishop
  | knight
  | pawn
deriving DecidableEq

/-- A piece: a colour and a kind. -/
structure Piece where
  color : Color
  type : PieceType
deriving DecidableEq

/-- A square of the chessboard. Files `a, …, h` and ranks `1, …, 8` are numbered `0, …, 7`,
so `⟨0, 0⟩` is `a1` and `⟨4, 0⟩` is `e1`. -/
structure Square where
  file : Fin 8
  rank : Fin 8
deriving DecidableEq

/-- The file displacement from `a` to `b`. -/
def Square.dFile (a b : Square) : ℤ := (b.file : ℕ) - (a.file : ℕ)

/-- The rank displacement from `a` to `b`. -/
def Square.dRank (a b : Square) : ℤ := (b.rank : ℕ) - (a.rank : ℕ)

/-- `b` is a square adjoining `a` (Article 3.8.1). -/
def Square.IsKingStep (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  max |a.dFile b| |a.dRank b| = 1

/-- `b` is one of the squares nearest to `a` that is not on the same rank, file or diagonal
(Article 3.6). -/
def Square.IsKnightJump (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  |a.dFile b| * |a.dRank b| = 2

/-- `a` and `b` are distinct squares on the same file or rank (Article 3.3). -/
def Square.IsRookLine (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  a ≠ b ∧ (a.dFile b = 0 ∨ a.dRank b = 0)

/-- `a` and `b` are distinct squares on the same diagonal (Article 3.2). -/
def Square.IsBishopLine (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  a ≠ b ∧ |a.dFile b| = |a.dRank b|

/-- `s` lies strictly between `a` and `b` on the line through `a` and `b`. -/
def Square.IsBetween (a b s : Square) : Prop :=
  ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ (k : ℤ) < max |a.dFile b| |a.dRank b| ∧
    a.dFile s = k * (a.dFile b).sign ∧ a.dRank s = k * (a.dRank b).sign

/-- The contents of the board: the piece occupying each square, if any. -/
abbrev Board := Square → Option Piece

/-- No piece stands strictly between `a` and `b` (Article 3.5). -/
def Board.PathClear (B : Board) (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  ∀ s, a.IsBetween b s → B s = none

/-- The piece `p` standing on `a` attacks the square `b` (Articles 3.1.2, 3.1.3): it could
capture on `b` according to the movement rules of its kind, regardless of what occupies `b` and
regardless of any check to its own king. -/
def Board.PieceAttacks (B : Board) (p : Piece) (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  match p.type with
  | .king => a.IsKingStep b
  | .queen => (a.IsRookLine b ∨ a.IsBishopLine b) ∧ B.PathClear a b
  | .rook => a.IsRookLine b ∧ B.PathClear a b
  | .bishop => a.IsBishopLine b ∧ B.PathClear a b
  | .knight => a.IsKnightJump b
  | .pawn => |a.dFile b| = 1 ∧ a.dRank b = p.color.forward

/-- Some piece of colour `c` attacks the square `b`. -/
def Board.Attacks (B : Board) (c : Color) (b : Square) : Prop :=
  ∃ a p, B a = some p ∧ p.color = c ∧ B.PieceAttacks p a b

/-- The king of colour `c` is in check (Article 3.9.1). -/
def Board.InCheck (B : Board) (c : Color) : Prop :=
  ∃ k, B k = some ⟨c, .king⟩ ∧ B.Attacks c.other k

/-- The two wings on which one can castle. -/
inductive Wing
  | kingside
  | queenside
deriving DecidableEq

/-- The original file of the rook used when castling on a wing. -/
def Wing.rookFile : Wing → Fin 8
  | .kingside => 7
  | .queenside => 0

/-- The file on which the king arrives when castling on a wing. -/
def Wing.kingTargetFile : Wing → Fin 8
  | .kingside => 6
  | .queenside => 2

/-- The file on which the rook arrives when castling on a wing. This is the file of the square
crossed by the king. -/
def Wing.rookTargetFile : Wing → Fin 8
  | .kingside => 5
  | .queenside => 3

/-- A position: the board, the player to move, the castling rights and the square on which an
en passant capture is possible on the coming move, if any. -/
structure Position where
  board : Board
  turn : Color
  /-- `castling c w = true` if player `c` still has the right to castle on wing `w`, i.e. neither
  the king nor the rook on that wing has moved (Article 3.8.2.1). -/
  castling : Color → Wing → Bool
  /-- The square passed over by a pawn that has just advanced two squares, if any
  (Article 3.7.3.1). -/
  enPassant : Option Square

/-- A move: the square of departure, the square of arrival and, for a pawn reaching the last
rank, the kind of piece it is promoted to. Castling is recorded as the move of the king. -/
structure Move where
  src : Square
  dst : Square
  promotion : Option PieceType
deriving DecidableEq

/-- The move `m` is a move of a pawn of the player to move, according to Article 3.7, ignoring
check: a single advance to an empty square, a double advance from the pawn's original square
over an empty square to an empty square, a diagonal capture of an opponent's piece, or an
en passant capture; a pawn reaching the last rank is exchanged for a queen, rook, bishop or
knight. -/
def Position.IsPawnMove (P : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  ((m.src.dFile m.dst = 0 ∧ m.src.dRank m.dst = P.turn.forward ∧ P.board m.dst = none) ∨
    (m.src.dFile m.dst = 0 ∧ m.src.rank = P.turn.pawnRank ∧
      m.src.dRank m.dst = 2 * P.turn.forward ∧ P.board m.dst = none ∧
      P.board.PathClear m.src m.dst) ∨
    (|m.src.dFile m.dst| = 1 ∧ m.src.dRank m.dst = P.turn.forward ∧
      ((∃ q, P.board m.dst = some q ∧ q.color = P.turn.other) ∨
        P.enPassant = some m.dst))) ∧
  (m.dst.rank = P.turn.promotionRank →
    ∃ t, m.promotion = some t ∧ t ≠ .king ∧ t ≠ .pawn) ∧
  (m.dst.rank ≠ P.turn.promotionRank → m.promotion = none)

/-- The move `m` moves a piece of the player to move according to Articles 3.1–3.7, ignoring
check. It is not castling. -/
def Position.IsPieceMove (P : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  ∃ p, P.board m.src = some p ∧ p.color = P.turn ∧
    (∀ q, P.board m.dst = some q → q.color ≠ P.turn) ∧
    (p.type = .pawn → P.IsPawnMove m) ∧
    (p.type ≠ .pawn → m.promotion = none ∧ P.board.PieceAttacks p m.src m.dst)

/-- The move `m` is castling by the player to move (Article 3.8.2): the king moves two squares
towards a rook of its colour on the first rank; the right to castle on that wing has not been
lost, there is no piece between the king and the rook, and neither the square of the king, nor
the square it crosses, nor the square it arrives on is attacked by the opponent. -/
def Position.IsCastling (P : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : Wing,
    m.src = ⟨4, P.turn.homeRank⟩ ∧ m.dst = ⟨w.kingTargetFile, P.turn.homeRank⟩ ∧
    m.promotion = none ∧
    P.castling P.turn w = true ∧
    P.board ⟨4, P.turn.homeRank⟩ = some ⟨P.turn, .king⟩ ∧
    P.board ⟨w.rookFile, P.turn.homeRank⟩ = some ⟨P.turn, .rook⟩ ∧
    P.board.PathClear ⟨4, P.turn.homeRank⟩ ⟨w.rookFile, P.turn.homeRank⟩ ∧
    ¬ P.board.Attacks P.turn.other ⟨4, P.turn.homeRank⟩ ∧
    ¬ P.board.Attacks P.turn.other ⟨w.rookTargetFile, P.turn.homeRank⟩ ∧
    ¬ P.board.Attacks P.turn.other ⟨w.kingTargetFile, P.turn.homeRank⟩

/-- The position after the player to move plays `m`. The piece leaves `m.src` and arrives on
`m.dst` (promoted if `m.promotion` is given); a pawn captured en passant and the rook used for
castling are moved accordingly. Castling rights are lost when the king moves and when a rook
moves from, or a piece moves to, the rook's original square. The en passant square is set after
a double pawn advance. The turn passes to the opponent. -/
def Position.play (P : Position) (m : Move) : Position :=
  let c := P.turn
  let moving := P.board m.src
  let arriving : Option Piece := match m.promotion with
    | some t => some ⟨c, t⟩
    | none => moving
  let isPawn := moving = some ⟨c, .pawn⟩
  let isKing := moving = some ⟨c, .king⟩
  let epCapture := isPawn ∧ P.enPassant = some m.dst
  let castle := isKing ∧ |m.src.dFile m.dst| = 2
  let wing : Wing := if m.src.file < m.dst.file then .kingside else .queenside
  { board := fun s =>
      if s = m.src then none
      else if s = m.dst then arriving
      else if epCapture ∧ s = ⟨m.dst.file, m.src.rank⟩ then none
      else if castle ∧ s = ⟨wing.rookFile, m.src.rank⟩ then none
      else if castle ∧ s = ⟨wing.rookTargetFile, m.src.rank⟩ then some ⟨c, .rook⟩
      else P.board s
    turn := c.other
    castling := fun c' w => P.castling c' w &&
      !(m.src = ⟨4, c'.homeRank⟩ ∨ m.src = ⟨w.rookFile, c'.homeRank⟩ ∨
        m.dst = ⟨w.rookFile, c'.homeRank⟩)
    enPassant :=
      if isPawn ∧ |m.src.dRank m.dst| = 2 then some ⟨m.src.file, c.passRank⟩ else none }

/-- The move `m` is legal in the position `P` (Article 3.10.1): it is a move of a piece of the
player to move or castling, and it does not leave the king of the player to move in check
(Article 3.9.2). -/
def Position.IsLegal (P : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  (P.IsPieceMove m ∨ P.IsCastling m) ∧ ¬ (P.play m).board.InCheck P.turn

/-- The player to move is checkmated (Article 1.4): the king is in check and there is no legal
move. -/
def Position.IsCheckmate (P : Position) : Prop :=
  P.board.InCheck P.turn ∧ ∀ m, ¬ P.IsLegal m

/-- The player to move is stalemated (Article 5.2.1): the king is not in check and there is no
legal move. -/
def Position.IsStalemate (P : Position) : Prop :=
  ¬ P.board.InCheck P.turn ∧ ∀ m, ¬ P.IsLegal m

/-- `Q` arises from `P` by one legal move. -/
def Position.Step (P Q : Position) : Prop :=
  ∃ m, P.IsLegal m ∧ Q = P.play m

/-- `P` is a dead position (Article 5.2.2): no series of legal moves leads to a checkmate. -/
def Position.IsDead (P : Position) : Prop :=
  ∀ Q, Relation.ReflTransGen Position.Step P Q → ¬ Q.IsCheckmate

/-- Two positions are the same in the sense of Article 9.2.2: the same player has the move,
pieces of the same kind and colour occupy the same squares, the castling rights are the same and
the possible moves are the same (in particular, the same en passant captures are possible). -/
def Position.Same (P Q : Position) : Prop :=
  P.board = Q.board ∧ P.turn = Q.turn ∧ P.castling = Q.castling ∧
    ∀ m, P.IsLegal m ↔ Q.IsLegal m

/-- The back rank of the initial position (Article 2.3). -/
def backRank : Fin 8 → PieceType :=
  ![.rook, .knight, .bishop, .queen, .king, .bishop, .knight, .rook]

/-- The initial position of the pieces (Article 2.3). -/
def initialBoard : Board := fun s =>
  if s.rank = 0 then some ⟨.white, backRank s.file⟩
  else if s.rank = 1 then some ⟨.white, .pawn⟩
  else if s.rank = 6 then some ⟨.black, .pawn⟩
  else if s.rank = 7 then some ⟨.black, backRank s.file⟩
  else none

/-- The initial position: White is to move and both players may castle on both wings. -/
def initialPosition : Position where
  board := initialBoard
  turn := .white
  castling := fun _ _ => true
  enPassant := none

/-- The state of a game: the current position, the number of half-moves played since the last
capture or pawn move, and the positions that occurred earlier in the game. -/
structure GameState where
  pos : Position
  halfmoveClock : ℕ
  history : List Position

/-- The state of a game at its start. -/
def initialState : GameState where
  pos := initialPosition
  halfmoveClock := 0
  history := []

/-- The state of the game after the move `m`. The half-move clock is reset by a pawn move or a
capture (including a capture en passant) and increased by one otherwise. -/
def GameState.play (s : GameState) (m : Move) : GameState :=
  let isPawn := s.pos.board m.src = some ⟨s.pos.turn, .pawn⟩
  let isCapture := s.pos.board m.dst ≠ none ∨ (isPawn ∧ s.pos.enPassant = some m.dst)
  { pos := s.pos.play m
    halfmoveClock := if isPawn ∨ isCapture then 0 else s.halfmoveClock + 1
    history := s.pos :: s.history }

open scoped Classical in
/-- The number of times the current position has appeared in the game (Article 9.2.2),
including the present occurrence. -/
noncomputable def GameState.occurrences (s : GameState) : ℕ :=
  1 + s.history.countP fun P => decide (P.Same s.pos)

/-- The possible outcomes of a game. -/
inductive Outcome
  | win (c : Color)
  | draw

open scoped Classical in
/-- The result of the game in state `s`, if the game has ended: the player who checkmated the
opponent wins (Article 5.1.1); stalemate (5.2.1), a dead position (5.2.2), the fifth occurrence
of the same position (9.6.1) or 75 consecutive moves by each player without a capture or pawn
move (9.6.2) are draws. Checkmate takes precedence over the 75-move rule. -/
noncomputable def GameState.result (s : GameState) : Option Outcome :=
  if s.pos.IsCheckmate then some (.win s.pos.turn.other)
  else if s.pos.IsStalemate ∨ s.pos.IsDead ∨ 5 ≤ s.occurrences ∨ 150 ≤ s.halfmoveClock
    then some .draw
  else none

/-- The player to move can claim a draw (Articles 9.2 and 9.3): the same position has appeared
for at least the third time, or the last 50 moves by each player were made without a capture or
pawn move, or the player has a legal move that produces one of these situations and claims the
draw together with that move. -/
def GameState.CanClaimDraw (s : GameState) : Prop :=
  3 ≤ s.occurrences ∨ 100 ≤ s.halfmoveClock ∨
    ∃ m, s.pos.IsLegal m ∧ (3 ≤ (s.play m).occurrences ∨ 100 ≤ (s.play m).halfmoveClock)

/-- `CanForceWin c s` holds if player `c` can force a win from the game state `s`: either the
game has ended with a win for `c`, or `c` is to move and has a legal move after which `c` can
force a win, or the opponent is to move, cannot claim a draw, and every legal move of the
opponent leads to a state from which `c` can force a win. -/
inductive CanForceWin (c : Color) : GameState → Prop
  | terminal {s : GameState} (h : s.result = some (.win c)) : CanForceWin c s
  | move {s : GameState} (h : s.result = none) (ht : s.pos.turn = c) {m : Move}
      (hm : s.pos.IsLegal m) (ih : CanForceWin c (s.play m)) : CanForceWin c s
  | opponent {s : GameState} (h : s.result = none) (ht : s.pos.turn = c.other)
      (hclaim : ¬ s.CanClaimDraw) (ih : ∀ m, s.pos.IsLegal m → CanForceWin c (s.play m)) :
      CanForceWin c s

open scoped Classical in
/-- The outcome of a perfectly played game of chess: `Outcome.win c` if player `c` can force a
win from the initial position, and `Outcome.draw` if neither player can. -/
noncomputable def perfectPlayOutcome : Outcome :=
  if CanForceWin .white initialState then .win .white
  else if CanForceWin .black initialState then .win .black
  else .draw

/-- The white king starts on `e1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem initialBoard_e1 : initialBoard ⟨4, 0⟩ = some ⟨.white, .king⟩ := by

/-- The black queen starts on `d8`. -/

private def last : Color → ℤ | .white => 7 | .black => 0

A drawn game-theoretic value is stated as the conjunction that White can force at least a draw and Black can force at least a draw. For this finite, deterministic, zero-sum game, this is the strategy-level formulation of value = draw.

The model uses current FIDE automatic termination by fivefold repetition and 75 moves, with checkmate taking priority, so completed optimal play is finite. Threefold repetition and the 50-move rule are player claims, including claims based on a declared intended move.
Resignation is modeled. Draw by agreement is omitted because it requires both players' consent and therefore does not change either player's forceable game-theoretic outcome.
Repetition equivalence compares board, side to move, castling rights, and only an en-passant target that gives rise to a legal en-passant move; the halfmove clock is deliberately excluded.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# First-move advantage in chess

What is the outcome of a perfectly played game of chess?

Chess is a finite two-player zero-sum game of perfect information, so by Zermelo's theorem
exactly one of the following holds: White can force a win, Black can force a win, or both
players can force at least a draw. Which one holds is not known. The consensus among players
and theorists (Steinitz, Lasker, Capablanca, Fischer, Kasparov, ...) is that chess is a draw
with best play; a minority view (Adams, Berliner) is that White can force a win.

No model of chess exists in Mathlib, so this file formalises the FIDE Laws of Chess from
scratch:

* `Board`, `Position`, `Move`: the pieces on the 64 squares, the side to move, castling rights
  and the en passant square; a move is given by its source and destination squares together
  with an optional promotion piece (castling is the two-square king move, en passant is the
  diagonal pawn move onto the en passant square).
* `Position.IsLegal`: the legal moves (FIDE Article 3), including castling, en passant,
  promotion and the rule that a move may not leave one's own king in check.
* `GameState.result`: the game ends with checkmate (Art. 5.1.1), stalemate (Art. 5.2.1),
  fivefold repetition (Art. 9.6.1) or the 75-move rule (Art. 9.6.2).
* `GameState.CanClaimDraw`: the player to move may claim a draw by threefold repetition
  (Art. 9.2) or by the 50-move rule (Art. 9.3), also with an intended move.
* `CanForceWin c s`: player `c` has a strategy from the state `s` that wins against every
  defence; a defender who can claim a draw is assumed to do so.
* `perfectPlayOutcome`: the game-theoretic value of chess from the standard initial position.

The following rules are omitted because they cannot change the game-theoretic value: draw by
agreement (Art. 9.1), resignation (Art. 5.1.2) and the dead position rule (Art. 5.2.2); from a
dead position no play can end in checkmate, so every continuation is drawn anyway. Rules about
clocks, arbiters and irregularities are not part of the mathematical game.

The 75-move rule makes the game finite: a game contains at most $96$ pawn moves and $30$
captures, and at most $150$ consecutive half-moves without either, so every game ends after a
bounded number of half-moves. Hence Zermelo's theorem applies and `perfectPlayOutcome` is a
draw if and only if neither player can force a win.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: First-move advantage in chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/first-move_advantage_in_chess)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia: Solving chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solving_chess)
- [FIDE Laws of Chess](https://handbook.fide.com/chapter/E012023)
- C. E. Shannon, *Programming a Computer for Playing Chess*, Philosophical Magazine 41 (1950),
  256–275.
-/

namespace FirstMoveAdvantageInChess

/- ### Pieces and squares -/

/-- The two players. White moves first. -/
inductive Color
  | white
  | black
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- The opponent of a player. -/
def Color.other : Color → Color
  | .white => .black
  | .black => .white

/-- The rank increment of a forward pawn move of colour `c`. -/
def Color.forward : Color → ℤ
  | .white => 1
  | .black => -1

/-- The rank on which the pieces of colour `c` start. Ranks 1–8 are numbered `0`–`7`. -/
def Color.homeRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 0
  | .black => 7

/-- The rank on which the pawns of colour `c` start. -/
def Color.pawnRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 1
  | .black => 6

/-- The rank on which the pawns of colour `c` promote. -/
def Color.lastRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 7
  | .black => 0

/-- The six kinds of pieces. -/
inductive PieceType
  | king
  | queen
  | rook
  | bishop
  | knight
  | pawn
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- A piece: a colour and a kind. -/
structure Piece where
  color : Color
  type : PieceType
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- A square of the board. Files a–h and ranks 1–8 are both numbered `0`–`7`; for example
`⟨4, 0⟩` is the square e1. -/
structure Square where
  file : Fin 8
  rank : Fin 8
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

namespace Square

/-- The file difference from `s` to `t`. -/
def dx (s t : Square) : ℤ := (t.file : ℤ) - s.file

/-- The rank difference from `s` to `t`. -/
def dy (s t : Square) : ℤ := (t.rank : ℤ) - s.rank

/-- The Chebyshev (king-move) distance between two squares. -/
def dist (s t : Square) : ℤ := max |s.dx t| |s.dy t|

/-- `s` and `t` are distinct squares on a common rank or file. -/
def OnRookLine (s t : Square) : Prop := s ≠ t ∧ (s.dx t = 0 ∨ s.dy t = 0)

/-- `s` and `t` are distinct squares on a common diagonal. -/
def OnBishopLine (s t : Square) : Prop := s ≠ t ∧ |s.dx t| = |s.dy t|

/-- `s` and `t` are distinct squares on a common rank, file or diagonal. -/
def OnLine (s t : Square) : Prop := s.OnRookLine t ∨ s.OnBishopLine t

/-- `u` lies strictly between `s` and `t` on a common rank, file or diagonal. -/
def StrictlyBetween (s t u : Square) : Prop :=
  s.OnLine t ∧ s.OnLine u ∧ (s.dx t).sign = (s.dx u).sign ∧ (s.dy t).sign = (s.dy u).sign ∧
    s.dist u < s.dist t

instance (s t : Square) : Decidable (s.OnRookLine t) := by unfold OnRookLine; infer_instance
instance (s t : Square) : Decidable (s.OnBishopLine t) := by unfold OnBishopLine; infer_instance
instance (s t : Square) : Decidable (s.OnLine t) := by unfold OnLine; infer_instance
instance (s t u : Square) : Decidable (s.StrictlyBetween t u) := by
  unfold StrictlyBetween; infer_instance

end Square

/-- The number halfway between `a` and `b`. It is the file of the rook's destination when
castling and the rank of the en passant square after a two-square pawn move. -/
def midpoint (a b : Fin 8) : Fin 8 := ⟨(a.val + b.val) / 2, by omega⟩

/-- The squares `t` that a piece of kind `pt` standing on `s` could move to on an otherwise
empty board (FIDE Art. 3.2–3.6). Pawns are treated separately. -/
def PieceType.Pattern : PieceType → Square → Square → Prop
  | .king, s, t => s.dist t = 1
  | .queen, s, t => s.OnLine t
  | .rook, s, t => s.OnRookLine t
  | .bishop, s, t => s.OnBishopLine t
  | .knight, s, t => |s.dx t| * |s.dy t| = 2
  | .pawn, _, _ => False

instance (pt : PieceType) (s t : Square) : Decidable (pt.Pattern s t) := by
  cases pt <;> unfold PieceType.Pattern <;> infer_instance

/-- The squares `t` on which the piece `pc` standing on `s` could capture, ignoring the other
pieces on the board. A pawn captures one square diagonally forward (Art. 3.7.3). -/
def Piece.AttackPattern (pc : Piece) (s t : Square) : Prop :=
  if pc.type = .pawn then s.dy t = pc.color.forward ∧ |s.dx t| = 1 else pc.type.Pattern s t

instance (pc : Piece) (s t : Square) : Decidable (pc.AttackPattern s t) := by
  unfold Piece.AttackPattern; infer_instance

/- ### Boards -/

/-- A board assigns to every square the piece standing on it, if any. -/
abbrev Board := Square → Option Piece

namespace Board

/-- No piece stands strictly between the squares `s` and `t`. -/
def PathClear (b : Board) (s t : Square) : Prop := ∀ u, s.StrictlyBetween t u → b u = none

/-- Some piece of colour `c` attacks the square `t` (Art. 3.1): it could capture on `t`, even if
it is pinned (Art. 3.1.3). -/
def Attacks (b : Board) (c : Color) (t : Square) : Prop :=
  ∃ s pc, b s = some pc ∧ pc.color = c ∧ pc.AttackPattern s t ∧ b.PathClear s t

/-- The king of colour `c` is attacked by the opponent (Art. 3.9.1). -/
def InCheck (b : Board) (c : Color) : Prop :=
  ∃ k, b k = some ⟨c, .king⟩ ∧ b.Attacks c.other k

instance (b : Board) (s t : Square) : Decidable (b.PathClear s t) := by
  unfold PathClear; infer_instance
instance (b : Board) (c : Color) (t : Square) : Decidable (b.Attacks c t) := by
  unfold Attacks; infer_instance
instance (b : Board) (c : Color) : Decidable (b.InCheck c) := by unfold InCheck; infer_instance

end Board

/- ### Positions and moves -/

/-- The two wings on which a king may castle. -/
inductive Wing
  | kingside
  | queenside
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- The initial square of the king of colour `c`. -/
def Color.kingSquare (c : Color) : Square := ⟨4, c.homeRank⟩

/-- The initial square of the rook of colour `c` on wing `w`. -/
def Color.rookSquare (c : Color) : Wing → Square
  | .kingside => ⟨7, c.homeRank⟩
  | .queenside => ⟨0, c.homeRank⟩

/-- The square on which the king of colour `c` lands when castling on wing `w`. -/
def Color.castleSquare (c : Color) : Wing → Square
  | .kingside => ⟨6, c.homeRank⟩
  | .queenside => ⟨2, c.homeRank⟩

/-- A chess position: the pieces on the board, the side to move, the castling rights and the
en passant square. -/
structure Position where
  /-- The pieces on the board. -/
  board : Board
  /-- The player who has the move. -/
  toMove : Color
  /-- `castling c w` holds when neither the king of colour `c` nor its rook on wing `w` has
  moved yet, and this rook has not been captured (Art. 3.8.2.1). -/
  castling : Color → Wing → Bool
  /-- The square passed over by a pawn that has just advanced two squares, if any
  (Art. 3.7.3.1). -/
  enPassant : Option Square
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A move: the square the moving piece leaves, the square it lands on, and the piece a pawn
promotes to (for promotions only). Castling is recorded as the two-square move of the king, and
an en passant capture as the diagonal move of the capturing pawn onto the en passant square. -/
structure Move where
  src : Square
  dst : Square
  promotion : Option PieceType
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

namespace Position

/-- The position obtained by playing the move `m` (the result is only meaningful when
`p.IsLegal m`). The moving piece leaves `m.src` and lands on `m.dst`, replaced by the promotion
piece if any; an en passant capture removes the captured pawn; castling also moves the rook to
the square the king passed over. Castling rights are lost by moving the king, by moving a rook
from its initial square and when a rook is captured on its initial square. -/
def play (p : Position) (m : Move) : Position :=
  match p.board m.src with
  | none => p
  | some pc =>
    let placed : Piece := match m.promotion with
      | some q => ⟨pc.color, q⟩
      | none => pc
    let b₁ : Board := Function.update (Function.update p.board m.src none) m.dst (some placed)
    let b₂ : Board :=
      if pc.type = .pawn ∧ p.enPassant = some m.dst then
        Function.update b₁ ⟨m.dst.file, m.src.rank⟩ none
      else b₁
    let b₃ : Board :=
      if pc.type = .king ∧ |m.src.dx m.dst| = 2 then
        Function.update
          (Function.update b₂ ⟨if m.src.file < m.dst.file then 7 else 0, m.src.rank⟩ none)
          ⟨midpoint m.src.file m.dst.file, m.src.rank⟩ (some ⟨pc.color, .rook⟩)
      else b₂
    { board := b₃
      toMove := pc.color.other
      castling := fun c w => p.castling c w &&
        decide (m.src ≠ c.kingSquare ∧ m.src ≠ c.rookSquare w ∧ m.dst ≠ c.rookSquare w)
      enPassant :=
        if pc.type = .pawn ∧ |m.src.dy m.dst| = 2 then
          some ⟨m.src.file, midpoint m.src.rank m.dst.rank⟩
        else none }

/-- The move `m` of a pawn of the side to move is a pawn move (Art. 3.7): one square forward to
an empty square; two squares forward from the pawn's initial rank over an empty square to an
empty square; or one square diagonally forward, capturing a piece there or capturing en passant.
A pawn reaching the last rank must promote to a queen, rook, bishop or knight. -/
def PawnMove (p : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  ((m.src.dx m.dst = 0 ∧ p.board m.dst = none ∧
      (m.src.dy m.dst = p.toMove.forward ∨
        (m.src.dy m.dst = 2 * p.toMove.forward ∧ m.src.rank = p.toMove.pawnRank ∧
          p.board.PathClear m.src m.dst))) ∨
    (|m.src.dx m.dst| = 1 ∧ m.src.dy m.dst = p.toMove.forward ∧
      (p.board m.dst ≠ none ∨ p.enPassant = some m.dst))) ∧
  (m.promotion = none ↔ m.dst.rank ≠ p.toMove.lastRank) ∧
  ∀ q, m.promotion = some q → q ≠ .king ∧ q ≠ .pawn

/-- The move `m` is a castling move of the side to move (Art. 3.8.2): the king moves from its
initial square two squares towards a rook of the same colour on its initial square, neither of
which has moved (the castling right is intact); all squares between the king and the rook are
empty; and the king does not stand on, pass over or land on a square attacked by the opponent.
-/
def Castles (p : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  ∃ w, m.src = p.toMove.kingSquare ∧ m.dst = p.toMove.castleSquare w ∧
    p.castling p.toMove w = true ∧
    p.board (p.toMove.rookSquare w) = some ⟨p.toMove, .rook⟩ ∧
    p.board.PathClear m.src (p.toMove.rookSquare w) ∧
    ∀ u, u = m.src ∨ m.src.StrictlyBetween m.dst u ∨ u = m.dst →
      ¬ p.board.Attacks p.toMove.other u

/-- The move `m` is legal in the position `p` (Art. 3): it moves a piece of the side to move to
a square not occupied by a piece of the same colour, following the movement rules of the piece
(with a clear path for queens, rooks and bishops), or it is a castling move or a pawn move;
only pawns promote; and the king of the side to move is not left in check (Art. 3.9.2). -/
def IsLegal (p : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  ∃ pc, p.board m.src = some pc ∧ pc.color = p.toMove ∧
    (∀ q, p.board m.dst = some q → q.color ≠ p.toMove) ∧
    (if pc.type = .pawn then p.PawnMove m
      else m.promotion = none ∧
        ((pc.type.Pattern m.src m.dst ∧ p.board.PathClear m.src m.dst) ∨
          (pc.type = .king ∧ p.Castles m))) ∧
    ¬ (p.play m).board.InCheck p.toMove

/-- Two positions are the same in the sense of Art. 9.2.2: the same player has the move, the
same pieces occupy the same squares, the castling rights are the same, and the possible moves
are the same (which accounts for en passant captures). -/
def Same (p q : Position) : Prop :=
  p.board = q.board ∧ p.toMove = q.toMove ∧ p.castling = q.castling ∧
    ∀ m, p.IsLegal m ↔ q.IsLegal m

instance (p : Position) (m : Move) : Decidable (p.PawnMove m) := by unfold PawnMove; infer_instance
instance (p : Position) (m : Move) : Decidable (p.Castles m) := by unfold Castles; infer_instance
instance (p : Position) (m : Move) : Decidable (p.IsLegal m) := by unfold IsLegal; infer_instance
instance (p q : Position) : Decidable (p.Same q) := by unfold Same; infer_instance

end Position

/- ### Games -/

/-- The possible results of a game. -/
inductive Outcome
  | win (c : Color)
  | draw
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The state of a game: the current position, the positions that occurred earlier in the game,
and the number of half-moves since the last capture or pawn move. -/
structure GameState where
  /-- The current position. -/
  pos : Position
  /-- The positions that occurred earlier in the game, most recent first. -/
  past : List Position
  /-- The number of half-moves played since the last capture or pawn move. -/
  halfmoveClock : ℕ

namespace GameState

/-- The state after the move `m` is played. -/
def play (s : GameState) (m : Move) : GameState where
  pos := s.pos.play m
  past := s.pos :: s.past
  halfmoveClock :=
    if (∃ pc, s.pos.board m.src = some pc ∧ pc.type = .pawn) ∨ s.pos.board m.dst ≠ none then
      0
    else s.halfmoveClock + 1

/-- The number of times the current position has appeared in the game (Art. 9.2.2). -/
def repetitions (s : GameState) : ℕ := (s.past.countP fun q => decide (s.pos.Same q)) + 1

/-- The result of the game if it has ended in the state `s` (Art. 5 and 9.6). The side to move
has no legal move exactly when it is checkmated, if its king is in check, or stalemated, if not.
Otherwise the game is drawn if the same position has appeared at least five times or if the
last 75 moves by each player were made without a capture or pawn move. -/
def result (s : GameState) : Option Outcome :=
  if ∀ m, ¬ s.pos.IsLegal m then
    if s.pos.board.InCheck s.pos.toMove then some (.win s.pos.toMove.other) else some .draw
  else if 5 ≤ s.repetitions ∨ 150 ≤ s.halfmoveClock then some .draw
  else none

/-- The player to move may claim a draw (Art. 9.2 and 9.3): the same position has appeared at
least three times, or the last 50 moves by each player were made without a capture or pawn move,
or the player has a legal move after which one of these holds. -/
def CanClaimDraw (s : GameState) : Prop :=
  3 ≤ s.repetitions ∨ 100 ≤ s.halfmoveClock ∨
    ∃ m, s.pos.IsLegal m ∧ (3 ≤ (s.play m).repetitions ∨ 100 ≤ (s.play m).halfmoveClock)

instance (s : GameState) : Decidable s.CanClaimDraw := by unfold CanClaimDraw; infer_instance

end GameState

/-- `CanForceWin c s` means that player `c` has a strategy that wins the game from the state `s`
against every play of the opponent. As the least predicate closed under the three rules below,
it holds exactly when `c` can force a win in finitely many moves: either the game has ended with
a win for `c`; or `c` is to move and some legal move leads to a state from which `c` can force a
win; or the opponent is to move, cannot claim a draw, and every legal reply leads to a state from
which `c` can force a win. A player who can claim a draw is assumed to do so when it prevents a
loss, and a player who is trying to win never claims a draw. -/
inductive CanForceWin (c : Color) : GameState → Prop
  | won {s : GameState} : s.result = some (.win c) → CanForceWin c s
  | move {s : GameState} (m : Move) : s.result = none → s.pos.toMove = c → s.pos.IsLegal m →
      CanForceWin c (s.play m) → CanForceWin c s
  | reply {s : GameState} : s.result = none → s.pos.toMove = c.other → ¬ s.CanClaimDraw →
      (∀ m, s.pos.IsLegal m → CanForceWin c (s.play m)) → CanForceWin c s

/-- The pieces on the first rank in the initial position, from the a-file to the h-file. -/
def backRank : Fin 8 → PieceType
  | 0 => .rook
  | 1 => .knight
  | 2 => .bishop
  | 3 => .queen
  | 4 => .king
  | 5 => .bishop
  | 6 => .knight
  | 7 => .rook

/-- The initial position (Art. 2.3): White has the move, both players have both castling rights,
and there is no en passant square. -/
def initialPosition : Position where
  board s :=
    if s.rank = 0 then some ⟨.white, backRank s.file⟩
    else if s.rank = 1 then some ⟨.white, .pawn⟩
    else if s.rank = 6 then some ⟨.black, .pawn⟩
    else if s.rank = 7 then some ⟨.black, backRank s.file⟩
    else none
  toMove := .white
  castling _ _ := true
  enPassant := none

/-- The state at the start of a game. -/
def initialState : GameState where
  pos := initialPosition
  past := []
  halfmoveClock := 0

open scoped Classical in
/-- The outcome of chess under perfect play: White wins if White can force a win, Black wins if
Black can force a win, and otherwise the game is a draw. Since chess is a finite game, by
Zermelo's theorem exactly one of these three cases occurs, and in the last case both players
can force at least a draw. -/
noncomputable def perfectPlayOutcome : Outcome :=
  if CanForceWin .white initialState then .win .white
  else if CanForceWin .black initialState then .win .black
  else .draw

/-- White has exactly $20$ legal moves in the initial position. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem card_filter_isLegal_initialPosition :
    (Finset.univ.filter initialPosition.IsLegal).card = 20 := by
  native_decide

/-- The game has not ended in the initial state. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem result_initialState : initialState.result = none := by
  native_decide

/-- Fool's mate: after 1. f3 e5 2. g4 Qh4# Black has won. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem result_foolsMate :
    ((((initialState.play ⟨⟨5, 1⟩, ⟨5, 2⟩, none⟩).play
      ⟨⟨4, 6⟩, ⟨4, 4⟩, none⟩).play
      ⟨⟨6, 1⟩, ⟨6, 3⟩, none⟩).play
      ⟨⟨3, 7⟩, ⟨7, 3⟩, none⟩).result = some (.win .black) := by
  native_decide

/-- After 1. Nf3 Nf6 2. Ng1 Ng8 has been played three times the game goes on, but the fourth
repetition makes the initial position appear for the fifth time and the game is drawn. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem result_knightShuffle :
    ((fun s : GameState => (((s.play ⟨⟨6, 0⟩, ⟨5, 2⟩, none⟩).play
      ⟨⟨6, 7⟩, ⟨5, 5⟩, none⟩).play

Omitted rules, with justification in the module docstring: draw by agreement, resignation and the dead-position rule (Art. 5.2.2) cannot change the game-theoretic value (from a dead position every continuation is drawn anyway); clocks/arbiters are not part of the mathematical game.

Game value: `CanForceWin c s` is an inductive (least fixed point) predicate, so it holds exactly when `c` can force a win in finitely many moves. `perfectPlayOutcome` is `win white` if White can force a win, else `win black` if Black can, else `draw`. The 'else draw' branch relies on chess being a finite game (75-move rule plus at most 96 pawn moves and 30 captures) so that Zermelo determinacy makes 'neither side can force a win' equivalent to 'both sides can force at least a draw'; this fact is stated in the docstring, not proved in the file. Equivalent alternative phrasing: `¬ CanForceWin .white initialState ∧ ¬ CanForceWin .black initialState` for the draw answer.

Position identity for repetition (Art. 9.2.2): same board, same side to move, same castling rights, and the same set of legal moves (this implements 'the possible moves of all the pieces are the same', so an en passant square only matters if the en passant capture is actually legal, and a pinned pawn does not count).

Castling rights are tracked as Booleans; a right is lost when the king leaves its home square, when the rook leaves its home square, or when a piece moves onto that rook's home square (capture).
