import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# First-move advantage in chess

*What is the outcome of a perfectly played game of chess?*

Chess (under the FIDE Laws of Chess) is a finite two-player game of perfect information: the
fivefold repetition rule and the 75-move rule end every game after finitely many moves. Hence
exactly one of the following holds for the standard initial position (Zermelo's theorem): White
can force a win, Black can force a win, or both sides can force at least a draw. Which of the three
is the case is unknown: chess has not been solved. The consensus among players and theorists
(Steinitz, Lasker, Capablanca, Fischer, Kasparov, Watson, Rowson, Short, ...) is that White's
first-move advantage is not large enough to win with perfect play, and that a perfectly played game
is a draw. A minority (Adams, Berliner) has argued that White has a forced win.

Mathlib has no model of chess, so this file formalises the FIDE Laws of Chess from scratch:
the board and the pieces, the movement of the pieces (Art. 3), check, castling, en passant,
promotion, checkmate, stalemate and dead positions (Art. 5), the draw claims a player may make
(threefold repetition and 50-move rule, Art. 9.2 and 9.3), and the automatic draws by fivefold
repetition and by the 75-move rule (Art. 9.6). Draw by agreement and resignation are omitted
because they never change the game-theoretic value; rules about clocks, illegal moves and the
arbiter are not part of the game tree and are omitted as well. The value of chess is defined through the
inductive predicate `CanForceWin`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, First-move advantage in chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/first-move_advantage_in_chess)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Solving chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solving_chess)
- [FIDE Laws of Chess](https://handbook.fide.com/chapter/E012023)
-/

namespace FirstMoveAdvantageInChess

/- ### Colours, pieces, squares and boards -/

/-- The two players (colours). White moves first (Art. 1.2). -/
inductive Color
  | white
  | black
deriving DecidableEq

/-- The opponent's colour. -/
def Color.other : Color → Color
  | .white => .black
  | .black => .white

/-- The direction (in ranks) in which the pawns of a colour advance. -/
def Color.forward : Color → ℤ
  | .white => 1
  | .black => -1

/-- The rank (zero-indexed) on which the pieces of a colour start: rank 1 for White, rank 8 for
Black. -/
def Color.homeRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 0
  | .black => 7

/-- The rank (zero-indexed) on which the pawns of a colour start (Art. 2.3). -/
def Color.pawnRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 1
  | .black => 6

/-- The rank (zero-indexed) on which the pawns of a colour promote (Art. 3.7.5.1). -/
def Color.promotionRank : Color → Fin 8
  | .white => 7
  | .black => 0

/-- The six kinds of pieces (Art. 2.2). -/
inductive PieceType
  | king
  | queen
  | rook
  | bishop
  | knight
  | pawn
deriving DecidableEq

/-- A chess piece: a colour and a kind. -/
structure Piece where
  color : Color
  type : PieceType
deriving DecidableEq

/-- A square of the board, given as `(file, rank)`, both zero-indexed: `(0, 0)` is a1, `(4, 0)` is
e1, and `(7, 7)` is h8. -/
abbrev Square := Fin 8 × Fin 8

/-- The file of a square, as an integer in `{0, ..., 7}`. -/
def Square.file (s : Square) : ℤ := s.1

/-- The rank of a square, as an integer in `{0, ..., 7}`. -/
def Square.rank (s : Square) : ℤ := s.2

/-- A board assigns to every square the piece standing on it, if any. -/
abbrev Board := Square → Option Piece

/-- Move the piece standing on `src` to `dst`, capturing whatever stands on `dst`. -/
def Board.movePiece (B : Board) (src dst : Square) : Board :=
  Function.update (Function.update B dst (B src)) src none

/- ### Movement of the pieces (Art. 3) -/

/-- The unit steps along which a rook moves. -/
def rookDirections : Set (ℤ × ℤ) := {(1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)}

/-- The unit steps along which a bishop moves. -/
def bishopDirections : Set (ℤ × ℤ) := {(1, 1), (1, -1), (-1, 1), (-1, -1)}

/-- `B.Slides a b d` means that `b` is reached from `a` by `k ≥ 1` steps in the direction `d` and
that all `k - 1` intermediate squares are empty on `B` (Art. 3.5). -/
def Board.Slides (B : Board) (a b : Square) (d : ℤ × ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ b.file = a.file + k * d.1 ∧ b.rank = a.rank + k * d.2 ∧
    ∀ (j : ℕ) (s : Square), 0 < j → j < k → s.file = a.file + j * d.1 →
      s.rank = a.rank + j * d.2 → B s = none

/-- `B.Attacks a b` means that the piece standing on `a` attacks the square `b` (Art. 3.1.3):
it could move to `b` according to its movement rules if `b` were occupied by an enemy piece,
ignoring whether this would expose its own king. Pawn moves that are not captures are not
attacks. -/
def Board.Attacks (B : Board) (a b : Square) : Prop :=
  ∃ p, B a = some p ∧
    match p.type with
    | .king => a ≠ b ∧ |b.file - a.file| ≤ 1 ∧ |b.rank - a.rank| ≤ 1
    | .queen => ∃ d ∈ rookDirections ∪ bishopDirections, B.Slides a b d
    | .rook => ∃ d ∈ rookDirections, B.Slides a b d
    | .bishop => ∃ d ∈ bishopDirections, B.Slides a b d
    | .knight => (|b.file - a.file| = 1 ∧ |b.rank - a.rank| = 2) ∨
        (|b.file - a.file| = 2 ∧ |b.rank - a.rank| = 1)
    | .pawn => |b.file - a.file| = 1 ∧ b.rank = a.rank + p.color.forward

/-- The square `s` is attacked by a piece of colour `c`. -/
def Board.IsAttackedBy (B : Board) (c : Color) (s : Square) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a : Square) (p : Piece), B a = some p ∧ p.color = c ∧ B.Attacks a s

/-- The king of colour `c` is in check (Art. 3.9.1). -/
def Board.InCheck (B : Board) (c : Color) : Prop :=
  ∃ s, B s = some ⟨c, .king⟩ ∧ B.IsAttackedBy c.other s

/- ### Castling squares (Art. 3.8.2) -/

/-- The two sides on which a king may castle. -/
inductive CastleSide
  | kingside
  | queenside

/-- The original square of the king of colour `c` (e1 or e8). -/
def kingHome (c : Color) : Square := (4, c.homeRank)

/-- The original square of the rook of colour `c` on the given side (h1/a1 or h8/a8). -/
def rookHome (c : Color) : CastleSide → Square
  | .kingside => (7, c.homeRank)
  | .queenside => (0, c.homeRank)

/-- The square the king crosses when castling (f1/d1 or f8/d8). -/
def kingTransit (c : Color) : CastleSide → Square
  | .kingside => (5, c.homeRank)
  | .queenside => (3, c.homeRank)

/-- The square the king occupies after castling (g1/c1 or g8/c8). -/
def kingCastled (c : Color) : CastleSide → Square
  | .kingside => (6, c.homeRank)
  | .queenside => (2, c.homeRank)

/-- The square the rook occupies after castling (f1/d1 or f8/d8). -/
def rookCastled (c : Color) : CastleSide → Square
  | .kingside => (5, c.homeRank)
  | .queenside => (3, c.homeRank)

/-- The squares strictly between the king and the rook before castling. -/
def castlingPath (c : Color) : CastleSide → List Square
  | .kingside => [(5, c.homeRank), (6, c.homeRank)]
  | .queenside => [(1, c.homeRank), (2, c.homeRank), (3, c.homeRank)]

/- ### Positions and moves -/

/-- A chess position, in the sense of Art. 9.2.2: the placement of the pieces, the side to move,
the castling rights and the en passant possibility. -/
structure Position where
  /-- The placement of the pieces. -/
  board : Board
  /-- The player having the move. -/
  toMove : Color
  /-- `castling c side = true` means that the king of colour `c` and its rook on `side` have not
  yet moved (and that rook has not been captured), so castling on that side is not permanently
  prevented (Art. 3.8.2.1). -/
  castling : Color → CastleSide → Bool
  /-- If the last move was a two-square advance of a pawn, the square that pawn passed over
  (the square on which it may be captured en passant, Art. 3.7.4); otherwise `none`. -/
  enPassant : Option Square

/-- A move (Art. 3 and 4.7): either a piece moves from `src` to `dst`, capturing whatever stands
on `dst` (and, for an en passant capture, the pawn behind `dst`), with `promotion` the piece a
pawn is exchanged for when it reaches the last rank; or the player castles on the given side. -/
inductive Move
  | normal (src dst : Square) (promotion : Option PieceType)
  | castle (side : CastleSide)

namespace Position

/-- The move `src → dst` is an en passant capture by a pawn of the side to move (Art. 3.7.4). -/
def IsEnPassantCapture (P : Position) (src dst : Square) : Prop :=
  P.board src = some ⟨P.toMove, .pawn⟩ ∧ P.enPassant = some dst ∧ |dst.file - src.file| = 1

/-- The move `src → dst` is a two-square advance of a pawn of the side to move (Art. 3.7.2). -/
def IsDoubleAdvance (P : Position) (src dst : Square) : Prop :=
  P.board src = some ⟨P.toMove, .pawn⟩ ∧ dst.1 = src.1 ∧
    dst.rank = src.rank + 2 * P.toMove.forward

/-- The move `src → dst` (with promotion `promo`) is allowed by the movement rules of the piece
standing on `src` (Art. 3.1–3.7), ignoring whether it leaves the own king in check. -/
def IsPseudoLegalNormal (P : Position) (src dst : Square) (promo : Option PieceType) : Prop :=
  ∃ p, P.board src = some p ∧ p.color = P.toMove ∧
    (∀ q, P.board dst = some q → q.color ≠ P.toMove) ∧
    match p.type with
    | .pawn =>
        -- the pawn advances one square to an empty square (Art. 3.7.1),
        ((dst.1 = src.1 ∧ dst.rank = src.rank + P.toMove.forward ∧ P.board dst = none) ∨
          -- or advances two squares from its original square over an empty square (Art. 3.7.2),
          (P.IsDoubleAdvance src dst ∧ src.2 = P.toMove.pawnRank ∧ P.board dst = none ∧
            ∀ s : Square, s.1 = src.1 → s.rank = src.rank + P.toMove.forward →
              P.board s = none) ∨
          -- or captures diagonally forward (Art. 3.7.3),
          (|dst.file - src.file| = 1 ∧ dst.rank = src.rank + P.toMove.forward ∧
            ∃ q, P.board dst = some q) ∨
          -- or captures en passant (Art. 3.7.4).
          (P.IsEnPassantCapture src dst ∧ dst.rank = src.rank + P.toMove.forward)) ∧
        -- A pawn reaching the last rank must be promoted to a queen, rook, bishop or knight
        -- (Art. 3.7.5); otherwise there is no promotion.
        (if dst.2 = P.toMove.promotionRank then
          ∃ t, promo = some t ∧ t ≠ .king ∧ t ≠ .pawn
        else promo = none)
    | _ => promo = none ∧ P.board.Attacks src dst

/-- Castling on `side` is not prevented (Art. 3.8.2): the king and the rook have not moved, they
stand on their original squares, the squares between them are empty, the king is not in check and
does not cross an attacked square. (That the king does not end up on an attacked square is part
of `Position.IsLegal`.) -/
def CanCastle (P : Position) (side : CastleSide) : Prop :=
  P.castling P.toMove side = true ∧
    P.board (kingHome P.toMove) = some ⟨P.toMove, .king⟩ ∧
    P.board (rookHome P.toMove side) = some ⟨P.toMove, .rook⟩ ∧
    (∀ s ∈ castlingPath P.toMove side, P.board s = none) ∧
    ¬ P.board.IsAttackedBy P.toMove.other (kingHome P.toMove) ∧
    ¬ P.board.IsAttackedBy P.toMove.other (kingTransit P.toMove side)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The position after the move `src → dst` with promotion `promo` (Art. 3.7.4, 3.7.5, 4.7):
the piece is moved, a pawn captured en passant is removed, a promoted pawn is exchanged, castling
rights are lost when the king or a rook leaves its original square or a rook is captured on it,
and the en passant square is recorded after a two-square pawn advance. -/
noncomputable def playNormal (P : Position) (src dst : Square) (promo : Option PieceType) :
    Position where
  board :=
    let B₀ : Board := if P.IsEnPassantCapture src dst then
      Function.update P.board (dst.1, src.2) none else P.board
    let B₁ := B₀.movePiece src dst
    match promo with
    | none => B₁
    | some t => Function.update B₁ dst (some ⟨P.toMove, t⟩)
  toMove := P.toMove.other
  castling c side := P.castling c side && decide (src ≠ kingHome c) &&
    decide (src ≠ rookHome c side) && decide (dst ≠ rookHome c side)
  enPassant := if P.IsDoubleAdvance src dst then
    some (src.1, ⟨(src.2.val + dst.2.val) / 2, by omega⟩) else none

/-- The position after castling on `side` (Art. 3.8.2). -/
def playCastle (P : Position) (side : CastleSide) : Position where
  board := ((P.board.movePiece (kingHome P.toMove) (kingCastled P.toMove side)).movePiece
    (rookHome P.toMove side) (rookCastled P.toMove side))
  toMove := P.toMove.other
  castling c side' := if c = P.toMove then false else P.castling c side'
  enPassant := none

/-- The position after a move. -/
noncomputable def play (P : Position) : Move → Position
  | .normal src dst promo => P.playNormal src dst promo
  | .castle side => P.playCastle side

/-- A move is legal (Art. 3.9 and 3.10.1) if it follows the movement rules and does not leave the
king of the moving side in check. -/
def IsLegal (P : Position) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  (match m with
    | .normal src dst promo => P.IsPseudoLegalNormal src dst promo
    | .castle side => P.CanCastle side) ∧
  ¬ (P.play m).board.InCheck P.toMove

/-- The move is a pawn move or a capture (this resets the 50- and 75-move counters, Art. 9.3 and
9.6.2). -/
def IsPawnMoveOrCapture (P : Position) : Move → Prop
  | .normal src dst _ => P.board src = some ⟨P.toMove, .pawn⟩ ∨ P.board dst ≠ none
  | .castle _ => False

/-- The side to move is checkmated (Art. 1.4.1 and 5.1.1): its king is in check and it has no
legal move. -/
def IsCheckmate (P : Position) : Prop :=
  P.board.InCheck P.toMove ∧ ¬ ∃ m, P.IsLegal m

/-- The side to move is stalemated (Art. 5.2.1): it is not in check and has no legal move. -/
def IsStalemate (P : Position) : Prop :=
  ¬ P.board.InCheck P.toMove ∧ ¬ ∃ m, P.IsLegal m

/-- A dead position (Art. 5.2.2): no series of legal moves leads to a checkmate. -/
def IsDead (P : Position) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ Q, Relation.ReflTransGen (fun A B : Position => ∃ m, A.IsLegal m ∧ B = A.play m) P Q ∧
    Q.IsCheckmate

/-- Two positions are the same in the sense of Art. 9.2.2: the same player has the move, pieces
of the same kind and colour occupy the same squares, the castling rights are the same, and the
possible moves are the same (this distinguishes positions by the en passant possibility). -/
def Same (P Q : Position) : Prop :=
  P.board = Q.board ∧ P.toMove = Q.toMove ∧ P.castling = Q.castling ∧
    ∀ m, P.IsLegal m ↔ Q.IsLegal m

end Position

/-- The pieces on the first and eighth ranks in the initial position, by file (Art. 2.3). -/
def backRank : Fin 8 → PieceType :=
  ![.rook, .knight, .bishop, .queen, .king, .bishop, .knight, .rook]

/-- The initial placement of the pieces (Art. 2.3). -/
def initialBoard : Board := fun s =>
  if s.2 = 0 then some ⟨.white, backRank s.1⟩
  else if s.2 = 1 then some ⟨.white, .pawn⟩
  else if s.2 = 6 then some ⟨.black, .pawn⟩
  else if s.2 = 7 then some ⟨.black, backRank s.1⟩
  else none

/-- The initial position: White to move, all castling rights available. -/
def initialPosition : Position where
  board := initialBoard
  toMove := .white
  castling _ _ := true
  enPassant := none

/- ### Games -/

/-- The state of a game: the current position, the positions that appeared before it (most recent
first), and the number of consecutive half-moves made without a pawn move or a capture. -/
structure GameState where
  /-- The current position. -/
  pos : Position
  /-- The positions that appeared earlier in the game, most recent first. -/
  history : List Position
  /-- The number of consecutive half-moves (moves by a single player) made without the movement
  of any pawn and without any capture. -/
  clock : ℕ

/-- The initial state of a game. -/
def initialState : GameState where
  pos := initialPosition
  history := []
  clock := 0

namespace GameState

open scoped Classical in
/-- The state after a move. -/
noncomputable def play (s : GameState) (m : Move) : GameState where
  pos := s.pos.play m
  history := s.pos :: s.history
  clock := if s.pos.IsPawnMoveOrCapture m then 0 else s.clock + 1

open scoped Classical in
/-- The number of times the current position has appeared in the game so far (counting the
current occurrence), in the sense of Art. 9.2.2. -/
noncomputable def occurrences (s : GameState) : ℕ :=
  ((s.pos :: s.history).filter fun Q => decide (Q.Same s.pos)).length

/-- The game is over: by checkmate (Art. 5.1.1), stalemate (Art. 5.2.1), dead position
(Art. 5.2.2), fivefold repetition (Art. 9.6.1), or because at least 75 moves have been made by
each player without the movement of any pawn and without any capture (Art. 9.6.2). -/
def IsOver (s : GameState) : Prop :=
  s.pos.IsCheckmate ∨ s.pos.IsStalemate ∨ s.pos.IsDead ∨ 5 ≤ s.occurrences ∨ 150 ≤ s.clock

/-- The player having the move may claim a draw (Art. 9.2 and 9.3): the same position has
appeared (or is about to appear after a legal move the player declares) for at least the third
time, or the last 50 moves by each player have been made (or will have been made after a legal
move the player declares) without the movement of any pawn and without any capture. -/
def CanClaimDraw (s : GameState) : Prop :=
  3 ≤ s.occurrences ∨ 100 ≤ s.clock ∨
    ∃ m, s.pos.IsLegal m ∧ (3 ≤ (s.play m).occurrences ∨ 100 ≤ (s.play m).clock)

end GameState

/-- `CanForceWin c s` means that player `c` can force a win (a checkmate of the opponent) from the
game state `s`, whatever the opponent does. It is the least predicate such that:
* `c` has won if the game is over and the opponent is checkmated;
* if the game is not over and `c` has the move, then `c` can force a win if some legal move leads
  to a state from which `c` can force a win;
* if the game is not over and the opponent has the move, then `c` can force a win if the opponent
  cannot claim a draw and every legal move of the opponent leads to a state from which `c` can
  force a win.

The game is drawn with perfect play if and only if neither player can force a win. -/
inductive CanForceWin (c : Color) : GameState → Prop
  | checkmate (s : GameState) (h : s.pos.IsCheckmate) (hc : s.pos.toMove = c.other) :
      CanForceWin c s
  | ownMove (s : GameState) (h : ¬ s.IsOver) (hc : s.pos.toMove = c) (m : Move)
      (hm : s.pos.IsLegal m) (ih : CanForceWin c (s.play m)) : CanForceWin c s
  | oppMove (s : GameState) (h : ¬ s.IsOver) (hc : s.pos.toMove = c.other)
      (hclaim : ¬ s.CanClaimDraw) (ih : ∀ m, s.pos.IsLegal m → CanForceWin c (s.play m)) :
      CanForceWin c s

/-- The three possible outcomes of a game of chess. -/
inductive Outcome
  | whiteWins
  | draw
  | blackWins
deriving DecidableEq

open scoped Classical in
/-- The game-theoretic value of chess: the outcome of a perfectly played game from the initial
position. It is `whiteWins` if White can force a win, `blackWins` if Black can force a win, and
`draw` if neither player can force a win (i.e. both players can force at least a draw). -/
noncomputable def value : Outcome :=
  if CanForceWin .white initialState then .whiteWins
  else if CanForceWin .black initialState then .blackWins
  else .draw

/-- Both players cannot force a win from the same state. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem not_canForceWin_white_and_black (s : GameState) :
    ¬ (CanForceWin .white s ∧ CanForceWin .black s) := by
  rintro ⟨hw, hb⟩
  induction hw with
  | checkmate s h hc =>
    cases hb with
    | checkmate _ h' hc' => rw [hc] at hc'; cases hc'
    | ownMove _ h' => exact h' (Or.inl h)
    | oppMove _ h' => exact h' (Or.inl h)
  | ownMove s h hc m hm _ ih =>
    cases hb with
    | checkmate _ h' hc' => exact h (Or.inl h')
    | ownMove _ h' hc' => rw [hc] at hc'; cases hc'
    | oppMove _ h' hc' hclaim ih' => exact ih (ih' m hm)
  | oppMove s h hc hclaim _ ih =>
    cases hb with
    | checkmate _ h' hc' => exact h (Or.inl h')
    | ownMove _ h' hc' m hm hw' => exact ih m hm hw'
    | oppMove _ h' hc' => rw [hc] at hc'; cases hc'

/-- The game has not ended in the initial position. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem not_initialState_isOver : ¬ initialState.IsOver := by
  sorry

/-- The move 1. e4 is legal in the initial position. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem initialPosition_isLegal_e4 : initialPosition.IsLegal (.normal (4, 1) (4, 3) none) := by
  sorry

/-- The move 1. Ke2 is not legal in the initial position. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem not_initialPosition_isLegal_Ke2 :
    ¬ initialPosition.IsLegal (.normal (4, 0) (4, 1) none) := by
  rintro ⟨⟨p, hp, hcol, hdst, _⟩, _⟩
  exact hdst ⟨.white, .pawn⟩ rfl rfl

/-- **First-move advantage in chess** (solving chess). What is the outcome of a perfectly played
game of chess, i.e. the game-theoretic value of chess from the standard initial position under the
FIDE Laws of Chess? Exactly one of the following holds: White can force a win, both sides can force
at least a draw, or Black can force a win. The consensus among players and theorists is that the
answer is `Outcome.draw`; a minority view is `Outcome.whiteWins`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 91]
theorem first_move_advantage_in_chess : value = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/-- The consensus conjecture (Steinitz, Lasker, Capablanca, Fischer, Kasparov, Watson, Rowson,
Short, ...): with perfect play chess is a draw, i.e. neither White nor Black can force a win from
the initial position. -/
@[category research open, AMS 91]
theorem first_move_advantage_in_chess.variants.draw : value = .draw := by
  sorry

end FirstMoveAdvantageInChess
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is appropriate: the question asks for the game-theoretic value of chess, and the 'White wins' minority view is just an alternative answer, not a separate sub-question. I followed the note's suggestion to make the game finite via the automatic 75-move and fivefold-repetition rules; in addition I included the FIDE draw claims (threefold repetition, 50-move rule) as player options, since a perfectly played game under FIDE rules includes the right to claim; this is recorded as a modeling decision a reviewer should check.
modeling_decisions: Rule set: the FIDE Laws of Chess. Modeled: piece movement (Art. 3), check, castling (rights + temporary prevention), en passant, promotion (to Q/R/B/N only), checkmate, stalemate, dead position (Art. 5.2.2, as 'no checkmate reachable by legal moves'), the automatic draws by fivefold repetition and the 75-move rule (Art. 9.6, with checkmate taking precedence), and the player's right to claim a draw by threefold repetition or the 50-move rule (Art. 9.2/9.3, including the 'declare the intended move' form). Draw by agreement and resignation are omitted (they never change the minimax value); clocks/illegal-move/arbiter rules are outside the game tree and omitted.

Draw claims are modeled as an option of the player to move: in `CanForceWin.oppMove` the opponent must be unable to claim a draw. Value-theoretically this coincides with the computer-chess convention that threefold repetition and the 50-move rule are automatic draws (the losing side always claims). A reviewer who wants only the automatic 75-move/fivefold rules (no claims) would drop the `hclaim` hypothesis; the main statement would otherwise be unchanged.

The value is defined via the inductive (least-fixed-point) predicate `CanForceWin c s` ('c can force checkmate in finitely many moves from state s') rather than by well-founded recursion on the finite game tree; `value` is whiteWins/blackWins if the respective side can force a win, and draw otherwise. Since chess (with 75-move/fivefold rules) is finite, Zermelo's theorem makes this the standard minimax value; the API lemma `not_canForceWin_white_and_black` (proved) shows the if-then-else in `value` is unambiguous.

Position identity for repetition (Art. 9.2.2): same board, same side to move, same castling rights, and same set of legal moves (this captures the en passant clause exactly, including the case where an en passant capture is geometrically possible but illegal). Occurrences are counted over the whole game, including the initial position and the current one.

Castling rights (`Position.castling`) are cleared when the king or the relevant rook leaves its original square, when a piece captures on the rook's original square, or when the side castles. Legality of castling checks: right present, king and rook on original squares, squares between empty, king not in check, transit square not attacked; the 'destination not attacked' condition is realized by the uniform 'own king not in check after the move' clause of `Position.IsLegal`.
The 75-move rule is `150 ≤ clock` and the 50-move claim `100 ≤ clock`, where `clock` counts consecutive half-moves without a pawn move or capture (en passant counts as a pawn move).

The statement is a question, so the slot uses `answer(sorry)` over `Outcome` (repository convention); the consensus 'chess is a draw with best play' is recorded as the variant `first_move_advantage_in_chess.variants.draw : value = .draw`.
Squares are `Fin 8 × Fin 8` as (file, rank), zero-indexed ((0,0) = a1, (4,0) = e1); the initial position is White to move with all castling rights and no en passant square.

Two `@[category test]` statements (initial state not over; 1.e4 legal) are left with `sorry` because their proofs require exhaustive attack enumeration; the Ke2-illegal test and the API exclusivity lemma are proved.
